definition_zh: 基础的；初级的；基本的；简单的；（科学）基本粒子的
definition_en: at the simplest and most basic level, dealing with first principles, or relating to the simplest particles of matter
core_image: 一年级教室的黑板上，写着 A B C 三个大写字母
scene: 乡村小学的教室里，孩子们跟着老师一遍遍念字母表。 She teaches at a small elementary school.
sceneCN: 这里 elementary 是「初级的、基础的」（第 1 个义项：指教育的最初阶段）；句意是她在一所规模不大的小学教书。

pos.zh: 形容词：基础的；初级的；基本的；简单的；基本粒子的

forms.label: 比较级（形容词，多音节用 more）
最高级（形容词，多音节用 most）

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉后缀 -ary 得到，义为「元素；要素」
与本词同源，由 element 加 -al 构成，义为「基本的；自然力的」
由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「基础地；简单地」
由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「基础性；简单性」

senses.title: At the first stage of school
senses.definition: relating to the first and simplest stage of education or training
senses.definitionCN: 指教育或训练的最初、最简单的阶段
senses.example: She teaches at a small elementary school.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一所规模不大的小学教书。
senses.why: The Latin -ary ending means belonging to, so elementary describes what belongs to the elements, the first things taught.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 -ary 词尾意为「属于」，所以 elementary 形容属于「元素」即最初所学之物的东西。

senses.title: Simple and easy to grasp
senses.definition: so basic that it needs no special knowledge, sometimes used to scold a careless error
senses.definitionCN: 基础到不需要专门知识，有时用来责备粗心的错误
senses.example: He made an elementary mistake in the first line.
senses.exampleCN: 他在第一行就犯了一个低级错误。
senses.why: What belongs to the elements is what every beginner already knows, so the word drifts towards simple and even too simple.
senses.whyCN: 属于「元素」的东西是每个初学者都已知道的，于是这个词滑向「简单」，甚至「简单得不该错」。

senses.title: Of the simplest particles
senses.definition: in physics, describing particles that are not known to be made of smaller parts
senses.definitionCN: 在物理学中形容尚未发现由更小部分构成的粒子
senses.example: Electrons are elementary particles.
senses.exampleCN: 电子是基本粒子。
senses.why: Physics returned the word to its oldest meaning: the unit you cannot split further.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把这个词送回了它最古老的含义：再拆不开的那个单位。

intro.en: Elementary is element plus the Latin adjective ending -ary; there is no e- prefix at all, and the word simply means belonging to the elements.
intro.cn: elementary 是 element 加拉丁语形容词词尾 -ary；它根本没有 e- 前缀，整个词的意思就是「属于元素的」。

items.en: Elementum named a first principle, the smallest thing you can teach or split.
items.cn: elementum 指第一原则，即你能教授或拆分的最小之物。

items.en: The ending -arius formed adjectives meaning belonging to, so elementarius meant of the elements.
items.cn: 词尾 -arius 构成「属于……」的形容词，elementarius 意为「属于元素的」。

items.en: French kept the adjective for what concerns first principles.
items.cn: 法语保留这个形容词，指涉及第一原则的事物。

items.en: English used it for basic teaching and for simple facts.
items.cn: 英语用它指基础教学与简单事实。

items.en: Schools, careless mistakes and physics particles all settled under the same adjective.
items.cn: 学校、粗心错误与物理粒子最后都归在同一个形容词下。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the element family straight; the near-meaning group separates basic, primary, fundamental and simple.
note.cn: 形近组理清 element 词族；近义组区分 basic、primary、fundamental 与 simple。

entries.definition: The noun this adjective is built on.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「元素；要素」，是本词的基干。

entries.definition: Of raw natural forces, with a stronger and older feel than elementary.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「自然力的；基本的」，比 elementary 更有原始力量感。

entries.definition: The adverb, rarely used outside technical prose.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「基础地」，多用于技术性文字。

entries.definition: Forming the base; the most common everyday word for this idea.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「基本的」，是这一概念最日常的说法。

entries.definition: First in order or importance; also used for the first years of school.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「初级的；首要的」，也用于小学阶段。

entries.definition: Serving as a foundation; heavier and more abstract than elementary.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「根本的」，比 elementary 更重、更抽象。

entries.definition: Not complicated; about difficulty, not about stages or particles.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「简单的」，说的是难度，而非阶段或粒子。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build the word straight from element plus -ary and then walk it from the first school year to the smallest particle.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把词直接拆成 element 加 -ary，再让它从小学一年级一路走到最小的粒子。

normal.en: No e- prefix here: element plus -ary, that is all.
normal.cn: 这里没有 e- 前缀：就是 element 加 -ary，仅此而已。

normal.en: Elementary school teaches the elements of reading and counting.
normal.cn: elementary school 教的就是读书与数数的「元素」。

normal.en: An elementary mistake is one a beginner should already avoid.
normal.cn: an elementary mistake 是初学者本就该避免的错。

normal.en: An elementary particle has nothing smaller inside it yet.
normal.cn: an elementary particle 里面至今找不到更小的东西。

normal.en: Same root as element, but the -ary makes it an adjective.
normal.cn: 与 element 同根，-ary 把它变成形容词。

abstract.en: Picture the first page of a textbook, all letters and dots.
abstract.cn: 想象课本的第一页，全是字母和圆点。

abstract.en: Whatever belongs to that first page is elementary.
abstract.cn: 凡是属于那一页的东西，都是 elementary。

abstract.en: Elementary is where a subject begins, and where physics ends its search.
abstract.cn: elementary 是一门学科开始的地方，也是物理停止追问的地方。

examples.en: She teaches at a small elementary school.
examples.cn: 她在一所规模不大的小学教书。

examples.en: He made an elementary mistake in the first line.
examples.cn: 他在第一行就犯了一个低级错误。

examples.en: Electrons are elementary particles.
examples.cn: 电子是基本粒子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「艾勒门特瑞」——小学黑板上那三个大写字母，就是一切的起点

root: 由 element 加拉丁语形容词词尾 -ary 构成，意为「属于元素的」；element 源自拉丁语 elementum，本词不含 e- 前缀。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of elementary: the first stage of schooling, what is too simple to get wrong, and the unsplittable particle.
sensesIntro.cn: elementary 的三个义项：教育的最初阶段、简单到不该出错的层次，以及不可再分的粒子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first page of a textbook, holding only letters and dots.
core.cn: 核心意象：课本第一页，上面只有字母和圆点。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: the first stage, taught from the elements.
branches.cn: 学校线：从「元素」教起的最初阶段。

branches.en: THE SIMPLE: basic enough that an error looks careless.
branches.cn: 简单线：基础到出错就显得粗心。

branches.en: THE PARTICLE: the unit physics cannot split.
branches.cn: 粒子线：物理学拆不开的那个单位。

branches.en: THE BEGINNING: what school teaches and what everyone should know.
branches.cn: 起点线：学校所教，也是人人都该会的。

branches.en: THE MINIMUM: simple in a book, simple in matter.
branches.cn: 最小线：书里的简单，与物质里的简单。

intro.en: Elementary is element plus -ary, from Latin -arius, meaning belonging to; there is no prefix involved.
intro.cn: elementary 是 element 加 -ary，来自拉丁语 -arius，意为「属于」；这里不涉及任何前缀。

latinIntro.en: Elementum and elementarius are recorded Latin forms; the adjective entered English through French.
latinIntro.cn: elementum 与 elementarius 是有记录的拉丁语形式；这个形容词经法语进入英语。

items.example: It is the base of this word.
It drops -ary to give the noun.

items.meaningCN: 磨损的拉丁词尾，并非后缀
items.example: It belongs to element, not to a suffix.
items.exampleCN: 它属于 element 本身，不是后缀。

definition_zh: 建造；竖立；竖直的
definition_en: to build something or raise it upright, or standing straight up
core_image: 一根柱子从地面被扶正，笔直地立起来
scene: 工人们在广场上竖起了一座纪念碑。 Workers erected a monument in the square.
sceneCN: 这里 erected 是 erect 的过去式，表示「竖立」（第 1 个义项：建造并使其立起）；句意：工人们在广场上竖起了一座纪念碑。

senses.title: To build or set up
senses.definition: to build a structure or set something upright in place
senses.definitionCN: 建造建筑物或把某物立起来安置好
senses.example: They erected a bridge across the narrow river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在狭窄的河上建了一座桥。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to raise up, so building and setting upright share one core action.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为向上竖起，因此建造与竖立共享同一个核心动作。

senses.title: To raise into an upright position
senses.definition: to lift or straighten something so that it stands vertically
senses.definitionCN: 把某物抬起或扶正，使其垂直立起
senses.example: The campers erected their tent before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 露营者在天黑前搭好了帐篷。
senses.why: The physical act of raising is the oldest layer of the word.
senses.whyCN: 向上抬起的身体动作，是这个词最古老的含义层。

senses.title: Standing straight up
senses.definition: standing or pointing straight upward, used as an adjective
senses.definitionCN: 笔直站立或指向上方，作形容词使用
senses.example: He sat with an erect back throughout the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 整个面试过程中他都挺直着背坐着。
senses.why: The past participle became an adjective describing the upright result.
senses.whyCN: 过去分词转化为形容词，描述竖立后的状态。

intro.en: Erect comes from Latin erigere, to raise up, from e-, out, and regere, to guide or keep straight.
intro.cn: erect 来自拉丁语 erigere（向上竖起），由 e-（向外）与 regere（引导、使直）构成。

items.en: Regere means to guide or keep straight.
items.cn: regere 意为引导或使直。

items.en: E- means out or upward here.
items.cn: 这里的 e- 表示向外或向上。

items.en: Erigere means to raise or set upright.
items.cn: erigere 意为竖起、使直立。

items.en: Erectus means upright or straight.
items.cn: erectus 意为竖直的、直的。

items.en: Erect enters English as verb and adjective.
items.cn: erect 作为动词和形容词进入英语。

items.en: Modern English uses erect for building and for posture.
items.cn: 现代英语中，erect 用于建造和姿态。

note.en: Erect is an upright word, close to its noun and adverb family and to verbs for building.
note.cn: erect 是表示「竖直」的词，与自身名词、副词词族以及表示建造的动词相邻。

entries.definition: the act of building or raising
in an upright way
a person or device that erects
to construct something
to lift or set upright
standing straight up

normalIntro.en: Erect is a raising word: a crane lifts a beam until it stands straight.
normalIntro.cn: erect 是「竖起」词：吊车把横梁吊起，直到它笔直站立。

normal.en: To erect a monument is to set it upright for people to see.
normal.cn: erect a monument 就是把纪念碑竖起来供人瞻仰。

normal.en: Workers erect scaffolding before painting a tall wall.
normal.cn: 工人在粉刷高墙前搭起脚手架。

normal.en: An erect posture means a straight back.
normal.cn: erect posture 指挺直的背。

normal.en: The noun erection can mean the act of building.
normal.cn: 名词 erection 可指建造的动作。

normal.en: Compare build: build is general, erect stresses standing something up.
normal.cn: 对比 build：build 泛指建造，erect 强调把某物立起来。

abstract.en: Picture a stone column rising slowly from the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象一根石柱从地面缓缓升起。

abstract.en: Imagine a flagpole pulled straight by ropes.
abstract.cn: 想象旗杆被绳索拉得笔直。

abstract.en: Think of a child standing tall to be measured.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子挺直身子量身高。

examples.en: The city erected a statue in her honor.
examples.cn: 这座城市为她竖立了一座雕像。

examples.en: They erected a fence around the garden.
examples.cn: 他们在花园四周立起了栅栏。

examples.en: He walked with an erect and steady gait.
examples.cn: 他走路时身姿挺直而稳健。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e + rect」——把弯的东西「弄直」，就是竖立；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 e-（向外）＋ regere（使直）→ erigere（向上竖起）→ erectus（竖直的）→ 英语 erect，核心义「使直立、竖起」。

sensesIntro.en: Erect begins with building and raising, then describes the act of standing something up, and finally the upright state.
sensesIntro.cn: erect 从建造与竖起开始，再描述把某物立起的动作，最后描述竖直的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a column lifted until it stands perfectly straight.
core.cn: 核心意象：柱子被扶起，直到完全笔直。

branches.en: Building and setting up is the main verb sense.
branches.cn: 建造与设立是主要动词义项。

branches.en: Raising upright is the physical action.
branches.cn: 使直立是身体动作。

branches.en: The upright state is the adjective sense.
branches.cn: 竖直状态是形容词义项。

branches.en: To erect a structure is to raise it into place.
branches.cn: 建造结构就是把它们立到位置上。

branches.en: Raising something results in an upright thing.
branches.cn: 把某物竖起，结果就是一件直立之物。

intro.en: Erect is a Latin raising word, with English relatives in erection, erectly, and erector.
intro.cn: erect 是拉丁语中表示「竖起」的词，英语亲属有 erection、erectly 与 erector。

latinIntro.en: Latin erigere means to raise up, from e-, out, and regere, to guide straight.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 erigere 意为向上竖起，由 e-（向外）与 regere（使直）构成。

items.meaning: a person or thing that acts

definition_zh: 在本地；在当地；局部地；在本机；在小范围内
definition_en: in or near the place where something happens, or in one limited part rather than as a whole
core_image: 同一条街上的菜摊、面包房与修车铺，货和人都来自不远的地方
scene: 周末的集市上，摊主把自家菜园里的蔬菜摆上木桌。 The tomatoes sold here are grown locally, so they reach the table hours after picking.
sceneCN: 这里是「在本地、在当地」（第 1 个义项：就在附近出产或发生）；句意为这里卖的番茄是本地种的，采摘几小时后就上了桌。可辨物件：木桌、成筐的番茄。

pos.zh: 在本地；在当地；局部地；在本机

derivatives.zh: 由 local 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「地区；街区」
由 local 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「使本地化；使局限于一地」
由 localize 加 -ation 构成，义为「本地化；定位」

senses.title: In or near the place where something happens
senses.definition: in the area where the speaker or the thing concerned is, rather than somewhere far away
senses.definitionCN: 在说话者或相关事物所在的这一带，而不是远处
senses.example: The fruit is grown locally and sold in the same town.
senses.exampleCN: 这水果是本地种的，就在同一个镇上卖。
senses.why: Local comes from Latin locus, a place, so locally simply says that something stays at or around the place in question.
senses.whyCN: local 来自拉丁语 locus（地方），所以 locally 就是「留在所说的这个地方及其附近」。

senses.title: In one part of the body only
senses.titleCN: 局部地；在身体某一部位
senses.definition: in a particular part of the body rather than through the whole body
senses.definitionCN: 作用在身体的某个部位，而不是通过全身
senses.example: The doctor applied the medicine locally to the sore knee.
senses.exampleCN: 医生把药涂在疼痛的膝盖局部。
senses.why: Because locus can also mean a single point or spot, the adverb can mark a small patch instead of a whole body.
senses.whyCN: 因为 locus 也可指一个点或一小块地方，所以这个副词可以只限定在一小块，而不是整个身体。

senses.title: On the machine you are using
senses.definition: on the computer or device in front of you rather than on a network or a remote server
senses.definitionCN: 在眼前的这台电脑或设备上，而不是在网络上或远程服务器上
senses.example: The files are stored locally, so they still open without a connection.
senses.exampleCN: 这些文件存在本机，所以没有网络也能打开。
senses.why: Computing borrowed the word for a place and used it for the place inside your own machine, as opposed to somewhere remote.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域借用了「地点」这个词，用它指你自己机器内部的位置，以区别于远端的位置。

senses.title: In a limited part of a whole
senses.definition: affecting or existing in only one part of a larger system or area
senses.definitionCN: 只在一个更大系统或区域的一部分中存在或起作用
senses.example: The damage is locally severe but the rest of the district is fine.
senses.exampleCN: 损失在局部很严重，但这一带其余地方还好。
senses.why: The same contrast between one place and the whole returns whenever an effect stays in one corner of a system.
senses.whyCN: 当一个影响只停留在系统的某个角落时，同一个「一处与整体」的对比就再次出现。

intro.en: Locally is the Latin place-noun locus turned into an adjective, then given the English adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: locally 由表示地方的拉丁名词 locus 先变成形容词，再加英语副词后缀 -ly 构成。

items.en: The Latin noun locus meant a place, a spot or a position, and it is the source of the whole family.
items.cn: 拉丁语名词 locus 意为地方、地点或位置，是这一整族词的来源。

items.en: The adjective localis, built on locus, meant belonging to a place, and English keeps its shape as local.
items.cn: 由 locus 构成的形容词 localis 意为「属于某一地方的」，英语保留其形，写作 local。

items.en: Old French used local for things of a place, and Middle English took the word from it.
items.cn: 古法语用 local 指与地方有关的事物，中古英语从这个词借入。

items.en: English added the adverb suffix -ly to local, making locally for something done at or near a place.
items.cn: 英语在 local 后加副词后缀 -ly，构成 locally，表示在某个地方或附近进行。

items.en: Modern English extends locally to body parts, to files kept on one machine, and to effects limited to one part.
items.cn: 现代英语把 locally 扩展到身体局部、存在单机上的文件，以及只影响一部分的情形。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin place stem; the near-meaning group collects adverbs that also answer the question where.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「地方」词干上的词；近义组收同样回答「在哪里」的副词。

entries.definition: Belonging to a particular place, especially one near you.
entries.definitionCN: 属于某一地方的，尤指就在你附近的。

entries.definition: A particular area or neighbourhood.
To find the exact place of something.
A place or a position.
At a short distance from here.
Within a particular region rather than across a whole country.
entries.definitionCN: 在某一地区范围内，而非全国。

entries.definition: Inside the country rather than abroad.

normalIntro.en: Locally is local plus -ly, and local goes back to the Latin noun for a place, so every sense keeps a sense of location.
normalIntro.cn: locally 是 local 加 -ly，而 local 又可追到表示地方的拉丁名词，所以每个义项都保留着「位置」的意味。

normal.en: Locally is local plus -ly, and local goes back to Latin locus, a place.
normal.cn: locally 是 local 加 -ly；local 又可追到拉丁语 locus，意思是地方。

normal.en: Anything done locally stays close to one place instead of spreading far.
normal.cn: 凡是 locally 做的事，都停在一个地方附近，而没有铺开很远。

normal.en: In medicine a drug applied locally works on one spot, not on the whole body.
normal.cn: 医学里说 locally 用药，是只在某一处起效，而不是全身。

normal.en: On a computer, locally means inside your own machine, the opposite of remote.
normal.cn: 在电脑上说 locally，指的是你自己的机器内部，和远端相对。

normal.en: Locally grown, locally made and locally sourced are fixed phrases on market signs.
normal.cn: locally grown、locally made、locally sourced 是集市招牌上的固定说法。

abstract.en: A place small enough to walk around in is the unit the word keeps returning to.
abstract.cn: 词反复回到的那个单位，就是小到可以走一圈的地方。

abstract.en: The word separates one point from the whole, which is why it fits both a sore knee and a single hard drive.
abstract.cn: 这个词把「一点」与「整体」分开，所以既能说膝盖的局部，也能说一块硬盘。

abstract.en: Locally is a quiet reminder that where a thing comes from is part of what it is.
abstract.cn: locally 悄悄提醒人：一样东西出自哪里，也是它本身的一部分。

examples.en: The vegetables on this stall are grown locally.
examples.cn: 这个摊上的蔬菜是本地种的。

examples.en: The cream is applied locally to the rash, not all over.
examples.cn: 药膏只涂在皮疹局部，不是全身抹。

examples.en: The backup is saved locally as well as in the cloud.
examples.cn: 备份既存在本机，也保存在云端。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「楼口里」——就在自家楼门口那一带，买本地菜最方便；记住 locally 是「在本地」。

root: 拉丁语 locus（地方）→ 形容词 localis → 古法语 local → 英语 local，再加副词后缀 -ly 成为 locally；同族词多与「地点、定位」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is being at or near a place; the other senses narrow that place to a body part, a single machine, or one part of a system.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是处在一个地方或附近；其余义项把这个「地方」缩小到身体某一处、单台机器，或系统的一部分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: market tables on one street, stocked by people and fields from just down the road.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一条街上的集市木桌，货和人都是从路那头不远处来的。

branches.en: market tables loaded with vegetables from fields a short drive away
branches.cn: 集市木桌上堆着从几里外菜地运来的蔬菜

branches.en: one corner of the district hit hard while the rest is calm
branches.cn: 这一带一角受损严重，其余地方安好

branches.en: a cream spread on one knee only
branches.cn: 药膏只抹在一个膝盖上

branches.en: files sitting on the laptop's own drive
branches.cn: 文件放在笔记本自己的硬盘里

branches.en: a small effect that stays inside one workshop
branches.cn: 只停在一个车间里的小影响

intro.en: The word is a Latin place-noun with two small English additions: an adjective ending and the adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个表示地方的拉丁名词，再加上两个小的英语附加成分：形容词词尾与副词后缀 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin locus supplies the place at the centre; localis turns it into an adjective, and English adds -ly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 locus 提供核心的「地方」；localis 把它变成形容词，英语再加 -ly。

definition_zh: 融化；熔化；消散；心软
definition_en: to change from a solid into a liquid under heat, and, by extension, to fade away or to lose hardness of feeling
core_image: 一小块黄油落在烧热的铁锅上，边缘先塌下去，摊成一圈亮亮的油
scene: 厨房里，一小块黄油落进烧热的铁锅，边缘先塌下去，转眼摊成一圈亮亮的油。 The last of the snow began to melt on the sunny side of the roof.
sceneCN: 这里 melt 是「融化、化开」（第 1 个义项：固体受热变成液体）；句意为屋顶向阳那一面的残雪开始化开。

pos.zh: 熔化后的食物；加奶酪的烤三明治

derivatives.zh: melt 的古老分词形式，专指高温下熔化的金属或岩石
由 melt 加 -ing 构成，义为「正在融化的」，也形容语气温柔
由 melt 与 down 复合而成，义为「熔毁」，也指体系或情绪的崩溃

senses.title: To turn from solid into liquid under heat
senses.definition: to change from a solid state into a liquid one, usually because heat reaches it
senses.definitionCN: 在热量作用下从固态变成液态
senses.example: The ice on the pond melted before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 池塘上的冰不到中午就化了。
senses.why: Old English meltan described a solid giving up its shape to warmth, so the physical change is the body of the word and every other sense borrows from it.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 meltan 说的是固体在温度面前交出形状，所以这个物理变化是词的身骨，其余义项都从它借力。

senses.title: To liquefy metal for casting
senses.definition: to heat metal until it flows so that it can be poured into a mould
senses.definitionCN: 把金属加热到能流动，好倒进模具里成型
senses.example: The smith melted the old coins and cast them into a bell.
senses.exampleCN: 铁匠把旧钱币熔化，铸成了一口钟。
senses.why: Metal needs a heat far beyond what butter or snow can take, so this sense narrows the same change to the workshop and the foundry.
senses.whyCN: 金属承受的热远超过黄油或雪，所以这个义项把同一种变化收窄到作坊与铸炉之中。

senses.title: To fade until nothing is left
senses.definition: to grow weaker and then vanish, as a crowd, a sound or a feeling does
senses.definitionCN: 像人群、声音或情绪那样越来越弱，直到不见
senses.example: The anger in her voice melted away once she saw the broken window.
senses.exampleCN: 她一看到碎掉的窗子，声音里的火气就散掉了。
senses.why: A melting thing loses its outline and spreads into what surrounds it, which is just what a crowd or a mood does when it stops having a shape you can point at.
senses.whyCN: 融化的东西失去轮廓、摊进四周，人群或情绪不再是一个能指认的形状时，做的正是这件事。

senses.title: To lose hardness of feeling
senses.definition: to stop being cold or firm in attitude and become gentle or sympathetic
senses.definitionCN: 态度不再冷硬，转为温和、体谅
senses.example: Her heart melted when the boy handed her the crumpled flower.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩把那朵揉皱的花递给她时，她的心一下就软了。
senses.why: Wax and ice go soft when warmth reaches them, and English uses that same softening of matter for a person whose coldness suddenly gives way.
senses.whyCN: 蜡和冰遇到温度就变软，英语便用物质同样的软化来形容一个人忽然放下冷硬。

intro.en: Melt goes back to an Old English verb for becoming liquid, and it has stayed close to that bodily picture ever since. No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for it.
intro.cn: melt 可上溯到古英语中表示「变成液体」的动词，此后一直紧贴那幅身体性的画面。这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.en: A reconstructed root often written meldh- is thought to have meant to soften or give way, but its exact shape is not certain.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个写作 meldh- 的构拟词根表示「变软、塌陷」，但确切形式并不确定。

items.en: The reconstructed verb meltanan carried the same idea into the Germanic languages, and its modern relatives still mean to melt.
items.cn: 构拟的动词 meltanan 把同一个意思带进日耳曼语族，它在现代各语言中的同族词仍表示「融化」。

items.en: Old English meltan meant to become liquid and could also describe a body or a thing wasting away.
items.cn: 古英语 meltan 意为变成液体，也可形容身体或物件渐渐消蚀。

items.en: Middle English kept melt for the physical change and began to use it for hard feelings that loosen.
items.cn: 中古英语的 melt 既保留物理变化，也开始用来指硬心肠的松动。

items.en: Modern English adds the noun melt, a dish topped with melted cheese, and keeps the figurative senses of fading and softening.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了名词 melt，指淋了熔化奶酪的热食，并保留「消散」与「心软」的比喻义。

note.en: The look-alike group holds forms and compounds built on the melting verb; the near-meaning group holds other words for turning soft or liquid, and for fading away.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在「融化」这个动词上的形式与复合词；近义组收其他表示变软、变液体以及消失的词。

entries.definition: Made liquid by great heat, said of metal, rock or glass.
entries.definitionCN: 被高温熔成液态的，多形容金属、岩石或玻璃。

entries.definition: In the process of becoming liquid, or soft enough to move someone.
entries.definitionCN: 正在化成液体的，也形容软到能打动人的。

entries.definition: A serious failure in which a core overheats, or any total collapse.
entries.definitionCN: 堆芯过热造成的严重事故，也指彻底的崩溃。

entries.definition: Grain that has been soaked and dried for brewing; it only looks like melt and comes from a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 泡过再烘干的酿酒谷物；只是拼写与 melt 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To become soft or liquid again after being frozen.
entries.definitionCN: 冰冻之后重新变软、化开。

entries.definition: To be absorbed into a liquid and lose separate form.
entries.definitionCN: 被液体吸收而失去独立的形态。

entries.definition: To make or become liquid, used mostly in technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 使变成液体，多用于技术性文字。

entries.definition: To make something less hard, or less severe in manner.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物变软，或使态度不那么严厉。

normalIntro.en: The word is native English, and its forms split between the ordinary past and an older participle kept for hot metal.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是英语本土词，它的各种形式分成了普通的过去式，以及专门留给高温金属的古老分词。

normal.en: Old English meltan already meant to become liquid, so the modern verb has barely moved in meaning.
normal.cn: 古英语 meltan 本来就表示变成液体，现代动词的意思几乎没有挪动。

normal.en: Melted serves as both past tense and past participle, while molten is the older participle that survived only for metal and rock.
normal.cn: melted 同时充当过去式与过去分词，molten 是只留给金属与岩石的古老分词。

normal.en: Melt down adds a downward particle and means to destroy something by melting it, which is why a reactor accident became a meltdown.
normal.cn: melt down 加了一个向下的虚词，意为把东西熔掉毁掉，反应堆事故因此被称为 meltdown。

normal.en: Melt in the mouth describes food so soft that the teeth are hardly needed.
normal.cn: melt in the mouth 形容食物软到几乎不用牙齿。

normal.en: Melt away uses away to show a shape thinning out until nothing remains to see.
normal.cn: melt away 用 away 表示轮廓一点点变淡，直到什么都看不见。

abstract.en: Anything that melts teaches the same lesson: hardness is only a temporary arrangement of warmth.
abstract.cn: 凡是能融化的东西都在讲同一件事：坚硬只是温度暂时给的一种排列。

abstract.en: A crowd melting away and a temper melting away share one picture, a shape that stops holding itself together.
abstract.cn: 人群散去和火气散去共用一幅画面——一个不再撑住自己的形状。

abstract.en: The word has no grand origin story, only a plain domestic change, and that plainness is why it works so well as a metaphor.
abstract.cn: 这个词没有宏大的来历，只有厨房里一个平常的变化，而正因为平常，它才这么好用作比喻。

examples.en: The snow melted as soon as the sun came out.
examples.cn: 太阳一出来，雪就化了。

examples.en: He melted the wax and used it to seal the letter.
examples.cn: 他把蜡化开，用来封住那封信。

examples.en: Her anger slowly melted away during the walk home.
examples.cn: 回家的路上，她的火气慢慢散掉了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卖它」——东西热到化掉，只好卖它换钱？记住 melt 是融化。

root: 古英语 meltan（变成液体），源自日耳曼语 meltanan，可上溯到构拟词根 meldh-（变软、塌陷）；无可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a solid losing its shape to heat. One branch stays literal and industrial, while the others follow the same loss of shape into fading and tenderness.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是固体在热中失去形状。一条分支留在字面与工业里，其余分支沿着同样的「失去形状」走向消散与温柔。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pat of butter collapsing at the edge of a hot pan.
core.cn: 核心意象：一小块黄油在热锅边缘塌下去。

branches.en: butter sliding down the side of a hot pan
branches.cn: 黄油顺着热锅边滑下去

branches.en: sparks and a crucible in a foundry
branches.cn: 铸炉里的火星与坩埚

branches.en: a crowd thinning until the square is empty
branches.cn: 人群一点点散尽，广场空了

branches.en: a hand going limp around a flower
branches.cn: 握着花的手慢慢松开

branches.en: a snowman losing its edges in the sun
branches.cn: 雪人在太阳下一点点失去棱角

intro.en: The word is a native verb with Germanic ancestry, and its shape is held by old endings that mark tense, an old participle and a downward particle.
intro.cn: 这个词是带日耳曼血统的本土动词，它的形态由标记时态的古老词尾、一个古老分词和一个向下的虚词共同撑起。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; its relatives are Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，它的同族词都在日耳曼语族里。

items.meaningCN: 过去式与过去分词词尾

definition_zh: 垂直的；竖的；纵向的；名词：垂直线、垂直方向
definition_en: going straight up and down, at a right angle to the flat ground or to a horizontal line
core_image: 一根铅垂线从屋檐垂下，线与地面严格成直角
scene: 木匠把线坠挂在刚起的墙边，眯眼一看，线垂得笔直。 The wall was not vertical, and the whole frame had to be reset.
sceneCN: 这里 vertical 是「垂直的」（第 1 个义项：与地面成直角、竖直向上向下）；句意为墙不垂直，整个框架都得重做。沿墙面垂下的铅垂线，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：垂直的；竖式的；纵向的

derivatives.zh: 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「垂直地；竖直地」
加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「垂直性；竖直程度」
同源自拉丁语 vertex「顶点」，义为「顶点；最高点」
加动词后缀构成，义为「使垂直；使纵向化」

senses.title: Straight up and down
senses.definition: going straight up and down, at a right angle to the horizontal
senses.definitionCN: 笔直向上向下，与水平面成直角
senses.example: A vertical line joins the top of the page to the bottom.
senses.exampleCN: 一条垂直线把页面顶部和底部连起来。
senses.why: Latin vertex means the top or the turning point at the crown; the vertical is the direction that points to the crown.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vertex 指头顶的顶点或转点；vertical 就是指向头顶的那个方向。

senses.title: Of an axis or graph
senses.titleCN: 纵轴的：图表中上下方向
senses.definition: relating to the axis that runs up and down on a graph
senses.definitionCN: 指图表中上下延伸的那一条轴
senses.example: Temperature is shown on the vertical axis of the chart.
senses.exampleCN: 图表的纵轴表示温度。
senses.why: On paper the ground is the horizontal, so height must be stacked upward along the other axis.
senses.whyCN: 在纸面上地面是水平线，高度就只能沿着另一条轴向上堆叠。

senses.title: Of a structure's shape
senses.titleCN: 竖立的：形容建筑或结构的形态
senses.definition: standing upright rather than lying flat, as of a wall, cliff or column
senses.definitionCN: 指墙、崖壁、柱子等立起而非平躺的形态
senses.example: The climbers faced a vertical wall of wet rock.
senses.exampleCN: 攀登者面对的是湿滑岩壁的垂直面。
senses.why: The abstract direction becomes a physical surface; to climb it is to go up the same line.
senses.whyCN: 抽象方向变成了实体的面；攀爬它就是沿着同一条线往上走。

senses.title: Of organisation or movement
senses.titleCN: 纵向的：组织层级或垂直起降
senses.definition: describing organisation or motion that works up and down a hierarchy, or straight up into the air
senses.definitionCN: 形容沿层级上下运作的组织方式，或笔直向上的运动
senses.example: The plane can make a vertical take-off from the narrow deck.
senses.exampleCN: 这种飞机能从狭窄的甲板上垂直起飞。
senses.why: The same geometric line now describes power and motion: straight up, with no sideways step.
senses.whyCN: 同一条几何线此时描述权力与运动：笔直向上，不向旁侧迈步。

senses.title: The noun: the upright direction
senses.titleCN: 名词：垂直方向或垂直线
senses.definition: used as a noun for a vertical line, surface or position
senses.definitionCN: 作名词使用，指垂直线、垂直面或竖直位置
senses.example: The shelf rests exactly on the vertical.
senses.exampleCN: 架子正好贴着垂直线安放。
senses.why: The adjective steps into noun use, as English often lets it: the upright itself.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转为名词用法，英语常常如此：指竖直本身。

intro.en: Vertical comes from Latin vertex, the crown of the head or the top point, which itself grew from the verb 'to turn'.
intro.cn: vertical 源自拉丁语 vertex，指头顶的旋或顶点，而后者又出自表示「转」的动词。

items.en: The verb vertere meant 'to turn'; a vertex is the point where something turns or peaks.
items.cn: 动词 vertere 意为「转」；vertex 就是事物转向或达到顶点的那一点。

items.en: Vertex meant 'whirlpool, crown of the head, summit, highest point'.
items.cn: vertex 意为「漩涡、头顶的旋、顶点、最高处」。

items.en: Late Latin verticalis meant 'of the highest point', and by extension 'overhead'.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 verticalis 意为「顶点的」，引申为「正上方的」。

items.en: Astronomers used the vertical for the line straight overhead; the exact first use in this sense is uncertain.
items.cn: 天文学家借用 vertical 表示正上方的直线；这一义项的确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Geometry fixed the modern sense: perpendicular to the horizon, the opposite of horizontal.
items.cn: 几何学确立了现代义：与地平线成直角，与 horizontal 相对。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the same vert- turning root; the near-meaning group gathers upright and perpendicular words.
note.cn: 形近组收同带 vert- 转根的词；近义组收表示竖直与垂直的词。

entries.definition: The top point or the corner where two lines meet.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「顶点」，指最高点或两条线相交的角点。

entries.definition: Lying flat, parallel to the horizon; the partner word that frames vertical.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「水平的」，与 vertical 相对而彼此定义。

entries.definition: Moral goodness; a different Latin word, easily confused in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「美德」，来自另一个拉丁词，拼写相近容易混。

entries.definition: Standing straight up; plainer and more physical than vertical.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「竖直的、站直的」，比 vertical 更朴素、更具体。

entries.definition: Meeting a line or surface at a right angle; geometric and precise.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「垂直的、成直角的」，更具几何精确性。

entries.definition: Exactly vertical, as checked with a weighted line.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「垂直的」，特指用铅垂线测得笔直。

entries.definition: Rising sharply, but not necessarily straight up.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「陡的」，形容坡面很斜，但未必竖直。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin vertex and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语 vertex，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: vertical pairs with horizontal: one stands, the other lies flat.
normal.cn: vertical 与 horizontal 相对：一个立着，一个平躺。

normal.en: vertex is the top of the head; vertical is the line that points there.
normal.cn: vertex 是头顶的旋；vertical 就是指向那里的那条线。

normal.en: On a chart, the vertical axis shows height and the horizontal shows time.
normal.cn: 在图表上，纵轴表示高度，横轴表示时间。

normal.en: Vertical take-off means up, straight up, without a runway.
normal.cn: vertical take-off 意为不靠跑道、笔直向上起飞。

normal.en: A plumb line hangs to tell you whether a wall is truly vertical.
normal.cn: 铅垂线垂下来，用来判断墙是否真正垂直。

abstract.en: Picture a weighted string hanging beside a new brick wall; the wall is right only when it hugs the string.
abstract.cn: 想象一条挂着重物的线在新砌的砖墙旁垂下；墙只有贴着这条线才是正的。

abstract.en: The word is defined by contrast: nothing is vertical alone, only against something level.
abstract.cn: 这个词靠对比来定义：没有东西能独自垂直，只能相对于某个水平面。

abstract.en: The same line runs through geometry, buildings and graphs: up is one direction only.
abstract.cn: 同一条线贯穿几何、建筑和图表：向上的方向只有一个。

examples.en: Draw a vertical line down the middle of the page.
examples.cn: 在页面中央画一条垂直线。

examples.en: The cliff is almost vertical for the last hundred metres.
examples.cn: 最后一百米，那面崖壁几乎完全垂直。

examples.en: The vertical axis shows the number of visitors each month.
examples.cn: 纵轴表示每个月的游客人数。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我（ver）提（ti）抠（cal）」——我提着一根线往下抠，看墙正不正：垂直的

root: 源自拉丁语 vertex「头顶的旋、顶点」，出自动词 vertere「转」，晚期拉丁语 verticalis「顶点的」；经科学拉丁语进入英语；同族词有 vertex、convert、version。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of vertical hold one line upright: a geometric direction, a graph axis, a standing surface, an upward movement, and finally the upright itself as a noun.
sensesIntro.cn: vertical 的五个义项守着同一条竖直的线：几何方向、图表轴、立起的表面、向上的运动，最后是作为名词的「竖直」本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plumb line hangs beside a fresh wall, and the wall is right only if it hugs the line.
core.cn: 核心意象：铅垂线在新墙旁垂下，墙贴着这条线才算正。

branches.en: GEOMETRY LINE: straight up and down, at a right angle to the ground.
branches.cn: 几何线：笔直上下，与地面成直角。

branches.en: GRAPH LINE: the height axis of a chart.
branches.cn: 图表线：图表中的高度轴。

items.en: Diploma named an official document of the state.
