definition_zh: 预防性的；预防的；预防措施
definition_en: intended to stop something from happening, or a measure taken for that purpose
core_image: 一辆检修车停在铁路边，轨道还没裂，工人已经在换那根旧螺栓
scene: 预防性检查在桥投入使用之前就发现了裂缝。 Preventive checks caught the crack before the bridge was used.
sceneCN: 这里 preventive 是「预防性的」（第 1 个义项：为阻止事情发生而做的）；句意：预防性检查在桥梁启用之前就发现了裂缝。图中可辨识物件：检修车、尚未裂开的轨道、换下的旧螺栓；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Serving to stop something
senses.definition: designed or intended to stop an unwanted event before it occurs
senses.definitionCN: 旨在在不受欢迎的事件发生之前将其阻止
senses.example: The school installed preventive barriers at the stairwell.
senses.exampleCN: 学校在楼梯口安装了预防性护栏。
senses.why: The -ive suffix marks function. Preventive describes what a measure is for, not what it has already done.
senses.whyCN: -ive 后缀标记功能。preventive 描述措施“为了什么”，而不是“已经做了什么”。

senses.title: Preventive medicine
senses.definition: the branch of medicine concerned with avoiding disease rather than treating it
senses.definitionCN: 关注避免疾病而非治疗疾病的医学分支
senses.example: Preventive medicine focuses on vaccination and screening.
senses.exampleCN: 预防医学侧重疫苗接种与筛查。
senses.why: Medicine splits by timing. Preventive work happens while the patient is well, which is why it is a separate branch.
senses.whyCN: 医学按时机分工。预防工作发生在病人还健康时，因此成为独立分支。

senses.title: Preventive measures
senses.titleCN: 预防措施：提前做的那几件事
senses.definition: countable steps taken in advance to reduce a risk
senses.definitionCN: 为降低风险而提前采取的可数步骤
senses.example: The report lists ten preventive measures for the factory.
senses.exampleCN: 报告为这家工厂列出十项预防措施。
senses.why: As a noun the word names concrete items, so a policy becomes a checklist of steps rather than a principle.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时它命名具体条目，于是政策变成一张步骤清单，而非一条原则。

senses.title: Preventive war
senses.titleCN: 预防性战争：趁对方还没强起来
senses.definition: describing war launched to stop an opponent from becoming a future threat, distinct from preemptive war
senses.definitionCN: 描述为阻止对手成为未来威胁而发动的战争，区别于先发制人的战争
senses.example: Preventive war is illegal under the modern law of conflict.
senses.exampleCN: 依据现代冲突法，预防性战争是非法的。
senses.why: The distinction is legal and precise: preemptive strikes answer an imminent attack, preventive war answers a distant one.
senses.whyCN: 这一区分是法律性且精确的：先发制人回应迫在眉睫的攻击，预防性战争回应遥远的威胁。

senses.title: Preventive detention
senses.titleCN: 预防性拘留：先关起来防出事
senses.definition: in law, detention ordered to stop a person from committing future harm rather than to punish past acts
senses.definitionCN: 法律上指为防止某人将来造成损害而非惩罚其过去行为的拘留
senses.example: Preventive detention raises serious human rights questions.
senses.exampleCN: 预防性拘留引发严重的人权问题。
senses.why: Law usually punishes the past. Preventive detention acts on the future, which is exactly why it is controversial.
senses.whyCN: 法律通常惩罚过去。预防性拘留作用于未来，这正是它受争议的原因。

senses.title: Preventive maintenance
senses.titleCN: 预防性维护：坏了之前先修
senses.definition: scheduled servicing of equipment based on time or use, before failure occurs
senses.definitionCN: 按时间或使用量在故障发生前安排的设备保养
senses.example: Preventive maintenance is cheaper than emergency repair.
senses.exampleCN: 预防性维护比紧急抢修便宜。
senses.why: Engineering splits maintenance into reactive and preventive. The adjective marks the version that acts before the breakdown.
senses.whyCN: 工程把维护分为事后与预防。这个形容词标记“在故障之前”的那一种。

senses.title: Preventive diplomacy
senses.titleCN: 预防性外交：别让争端打起来
senses.definition: diplomatic action taken to stop a dispute from becoming violent
senses.definitionCN: 为防止争端升级为暴力而采取的外交行动
senses.example: Preventive diplomacy kept the border talks alive.
senses.exampleCN: 预防性外交让边界谈判得以延续。
senses.why: Diplomacy borrows the medical word: conflict is treated like a disease that can be caught early.
senses.whyCN: 外交借用了医学词：冲突被视为一种可以早期发现的疾病。

senses.title: Preventive check
senses.titleCN: 预防性限制：经济思想里的旧词
senses.definition: in historical economics, Malthus's preventive checks are the limits people place on population growth themselves
senses.definitionCN: 在经济学史中，马尔萨斯的“预防性限制”指人们自行对人口增长施加的限制
senses.example: Malthus called delayed marriage a preventive check.
senses.exampleCN: 马尔萨斯把推迟婚姻称为一种预防性限制。
senses.why: The word was used long before medicine made it common, and this economic sense shows its general logic: act on the cause before the effect.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在医学让它流行之前就已被使用，这一经济学义显示了它的普遍逻辑：在结果之前作用于原因。

intro.en: Preventive is prevent plus -ive, from Latin praevenire 'to come before, forestall' (prae- 'before' + venire 'come').
intro.cn: preventive 是 prevent 加 -ive，源自拉丁 praevenire“先到、预先拦下”（prae-“在前”+ venire“来”）。

items.en: venire 'to come' underlies the family. Event, invent, intervene and convention all use the same stem with different prefixes.
items.cn: venire“来”是该词族的基础。event、invent、intervene、convention 都用同一词干，配不同前缀。

items.en: prae- 'before' plus venire gives 'to come before'. The practical sense 'to hinder' grows from arriving first.
items.cn: prae-“在前”加 venire 得“先到”。由于先到，实用义“拦住”生长出来。

items.en: -ivus in Latin marks capacity or function, so preventive means 'having the function of preventing'.
items.cn: 拉丁 -ivus 标记能力或功能，所以 preventive 意为“具有阻止的功能”。

items.en: English uses preventive first as a noun for a remedy that wards off illness, then as an adjective.
items.cn: 英语最早把 preventive 用作名词，指防病之物，随后用作形容词。

items.en: In the 19th and 20th centuries preventive medicine becomes the name of a whole branch of practice.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪，预防医学成为整个实践分支的名称。

items.en: The same adjective spreads to detention, war, maintenance and diplomacy, where the shared point is action before harm.
items.cn: 同一形容词扩展到拘留、战争、维护与外交，共同点是“在损害之前行动”。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ven- stem or the pre- prefix; the near-meaning group all act early, differing in whether they stop or prepare.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ven- 词干或 pre- 前缀；近义组都提早行动，差别在“阻止”还是“准备”。

entries.definition: the act or policy of stopping something. The noun names the effort; the adjective describes measures.
entries.definitionCN: 预防的行为或政策。名词命名努力，形容词描述措施。

entries.definition: an alternative form of preventive, common in speech and some writing. Both are accepted.
entries.definitionCN: preventive 的变体形式，口语和一些写作中常见，两者都被接受。

entries.definition: acting first against an imminent threat. It comes from pre- plus emere 'buy, take', not from venire.
entries.definitionCN: 先发制人的。来自 pre- 加 emere“买、取”，并非 venire。

entries.definition: describing treatment given to ward off disease. It is the clinical adjective for preventive in medicine.
entries.definitionCN: 预防性的。它是医学中 preventive 的临床形容词。

entries.definition: done to avoid possible harm. It stresses caution rather than a systematic programme.
entries.definitionCN: 防范性的。强调谨慎，而非系统性的方案。

entries.definition: describing something that shields from harm. It implies a barrier, while preventive implies earlier action.
entries.definitionCN: 保护性的。暗含屏障，而 preventive 暗含更早的行动。

entries.definition: able to cure a condition already present. It is the natural counterpart of preventive.
entries.definitionCN: 治疗性的。它是 preventive 的天然对照词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: -ive marks function, so preventive means 'doing the job of stopping'.
normal.cn: -ive 标记功能，所以 preventive 意为“承担阻止任务”。

normal.en: Preventive maintenance is the clearest everyday example: repair before the machine breaks.
normal.cn: 预防性维护是最清楚的日常例子：在机器坏之前先修。

normal.en: Preventive versus curative is a timing pair, not a quality pair.
normal.cn: 预防与治疗是一对时机词，不是一对质量词。

normal.en: Preventive war is legally different from preemptive war, and the difference is the distance of the threat.
normal.cn: 预防性战争与先发制人战争在法律上不同，差别在威胁的远近。

normal.en: Preventive detention is controversial precisely because it acts on the future rather than the past.
normal.cn: 预防性拘留之所以有争议，正因为它作用于未来而非过去。

abstract.en: Picture a mechanic replacing a bearing that still turns quietly.
abstract.cn: 想象机械师换下一个仍在安静转动的轴承。

abstract.en: Picture a fence put up while the field is still empty.
abstract.cn: 想象田里还空着时就立起的围栏。

abstract.en: Picture a doctor's appointment scheduled while the patient feels fine.
abstract.cn: 想象病人在感觉良好时预约的那次体检。

examples.en: Preventive treatment reduced the number of severe cases.
examples.cn: 预防性治疗减少了重症病例数。

examples.en: The airline follows a preventive maintenance schedule.
examples.cn: 该航空公司执行预防性维护计划。

examples.en: Preventive steps are cheaper, but they are invisible when they work.
examples.cn: 预防措施更便宜，但奏效时却看不见。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普瑞文提夫”音近 preventive：先“文”住口子、再“提”前防住——提前挡住不让发生 → preventive 预防性的

root: 拉丁 prae-“在前”+ venire“来”→ praevenire“先到、预先拦下”；prevent + -ive（拉丁 -ivus，表功能）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe measures that act before the harm, whether the harm is illness, war, crime or a broken bearing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述“在损害之前行动”的措施，无论损害是疾病、战争、犯罪还是坏掉的轴承。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bolt replaced before the rail cracks.
core.cn: 核心意象：轨道裂开之前换下的螺栓。

branches.en: FUNCTION AND ITEMS: the adjective describes the purpose, the countable noun lists the steps.
branches.cn: 功能与条目：形容词描述目的，可数名词列出步骤。

branches.en: MEDICINE: preventive work happens while the patient is well, which defines the branch.
branches.cn: 医学：预防工作发生在病人健康时，这定义了该分支。

branches.en: LAW: preventive war and preventive detention both act on a future harm, which is why both are contested.
branches.cn: 法律：预防性战争与预防性拘留都作用于未来的损害，因此都受争议。

branches.en: ENGINEERING: maintenance before failure is the industrial model of the same logic.
branches.cn: 工程：故障前的维护是同一逻辑的工业模型。

branches.en: SOCIETY: diplomacy and Malthus's checks apply the word to conflict and population.
branches.cn: 社会：外交与马尔萨斯的限制把词用于冲突与人口。

intro.en: Preventive is prevent plus -ive. The base carries 'come before', the suffix marks function, and the noun prevention carries the policy.
intro.cn: preventive 是 prevent 加 -ive。词基携带“先到”，后缀标记功能，名词 prevention 承载政策含义。

latinIntro.en: Latin venire 'come' → praevenire 'forestall'. English keeps vent- in prevent and adds -ive from -ivus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 venire“来”→ praevenire“预先拦下”。英语在 prevent 中保留 vent-，加 -ive（来自 -ivus）。

items.example: Prevention of sepsis is the priority.
items.exampleCN: 预防败血症是首要任务。

items.meaning: a device that stops a fault

items.example: The court intervened in the dispute.

definition_zh: 中断；打扰；打断的话；障碍
definition_en: the act of breaking in on something, a remark that breaks in, or a pause that stops a process
core_image: 会议记录上多出一行横线，把原本连贯的句子拦腰截断
scene: 孩子在书房门外探头，问了一句作业题，父亲只好放下笔。 After one interruption the speaker began again from the top.
sceneCN: 这里 interruption 是「打扰、打断」（第 1 个义项：打断别人的动作），句意为被打断一次之后，讲话者从头再讲。画面里的物件：门缝、作业本、笔。

pos.zh: 名词：中断；打扰；打断的话；障碍物

derivatives.zh: 去后缀构成，义为「打断；中断」
由过去分词构成，义为「被打断的」
加前缀 un- 构成，义为「不间断的」

senses.title: The act of cutting in
senses.definition: the act of breaking in on someone who is speaking or working
senses.definitionCN: 在别人说话或做事时插进来的动作
senses.example: He raised one hand to beg an interruption.
senses.exampleCN: 他举起一只手，请求插一句话。
senses.why: The noun names the snap itself, not the person who made it.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指那一次折断，而不指造成折断的人。

senses.title: A pause in a process
senses.definition: a break that stops an activity for a while and then lets it go on
senses.definitionCN: 使活动暂停一段再继续的间断
senses.example: Work continued for six hours without interruption.
senses.exampleCN: 工作持续了六个小时没有间断。
senses.why: Time made the break measurable: an interruption is now a gap on a clock.
senses.whyCN: 时间让这道断裂变得可以计量：中断成了钟表上的空档。

senses.title: A breaking remark
senses.definition: a remark or question that cuts into what someone else is saying
senses.definitionCN: 插进别人话语中的一句话或问题
senses.example: His interruptions made the lecture hard to follow.
senses.exampleCN: 他不断的插话让讲座难以跟上。
senses.why: From the act came the content: the words themselves are also interruptions.
senses.whyCN: 从动作派生出内容：那些话本身也被叫作 interruptions。

intro.en: Interruption is the Latin action noun built on interrumpere, to break in the middle.
intro.cn: interruption 是建立在 interrumpere（从中间打断）之上的拉丁语动作名词。

items.en: Rumpere meant to break a solid thing apart.
items.cn: rumpere 意为把坚硬之物折断。

items.en: Interruptio named the breaking of a continuous thing.
items.cn: interruptio 指打断一件连续之物。

items.en: Old French kept the noun for a break in speech.
items.cn: 古法语保留了这个名词，指话语中的打断。

items.en: English used interruption for halted talk, work, and travel.
items.cn: 英语用 interruption 指被打断的谈话、工作与行程。

items.en: Technology gave it the modern sense of service outage.
items.cn: 技术发展又添上「服务中断」这一现代义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -rupt stem; the near-meaning group holds other words for a break.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -rupt 词干；近义组收其他表示间断的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to break in.
The adjective meaning tending to interrupt.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「打断性的」，与 interruption 拼写相近。

entries.definition: A bursting out, as of a volcano.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「喷发」，同出 rumpere。

entries.definition: Something that upsets peace or order.
A pause between periods of activity.
A short stop with the intention to continue.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「停顿」，暗示还要继续。

normalIntro.en: These hooks turn the verb into something you can count on your fingers.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把动词变成能掰着手指数出来的东西。

normal.en: Add -ion to interrupt and the act becomes a countable event.
normal.cn: interrupt 加 -ion，动作就变成可数的事件。

normal.en: One interruption, two interruptions: each is a broken line.
normal.cn: 一次打断、两次打断：每一次都是一条断线。

normal.en: Without interruption is the wish behind every deep work session.
normal.cn: without interruption 是每次深度工作背后的心愿。

normal.en: An interruption to traffic annoys drivers more than a red light.
normal.cn: an interruption to traffic 比红灯更让司机恼火。

normal.en: Excuse the interruption is the apology before the cut.
normal.cn: excuse the interruption 是动刀前的道歉。

abstract.en: An interruption is a door someone opens in your sentence.
abstract.cn: 打断是有人在你句子里开了一扇门。

abstract.en: A day of interruptions is a day written in fragments.
abstract.cn: 被不断打断的一天，是用碎片写成的一天。

abstract.en: The noun weighs what the verb did.
abstract.cn: 这个名词替动词记下了那道切口的分量。

examples.en: The talk went on for forty minutes free of any interruption.
examples.cn: 讲座进行了四十分钟，一次也没被打断。

examples.en: Power interruptions left the street dark for a whole evening.
examples.cn: 停电让整条街黑了一整晚。

examples.en: Excuse the interruption, but the taxi is waiting.
examples.cn: 原谅我插一句，出租车已经在等了。

dict_mnemonic.text: interrupt（打断）+ ion（名词）——打断这件事本身

root: 拉丁语 rumpere「折断」→ interrumpere「从中间打断」→ interruptio「中断」→ 古法语 → 英语 interruption。同族有 interrupt、interrupted、uninterrupted。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the act of cutting in, a pause in a process, and the remark that does the cutting.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：插进来的动作、过程中的停顿，以及插进来的那句话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one stroke across a written sentence, cutting it in two.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句写好的话被一道横线拦腰截开。

branches.en: THE HAND: the raised hand that asks to cut in.
branches.cn: 举手这条线：请求插话的动作。

branches.en: THE CLOCK: hours run without a gap.
branches.cn: 时钟这条线：不间断的连续时段。

branches.en: THE WORD: the question itself that breaks the flow.
branches.cn: 话语这条线：打断连贯的那句问话。

branches.en: THE LINK: a cut and the words that made it belong together.
branches.cn: 连接线：那道切口与造成它的话是同一条线。

branches.en: THE COST: every remark costs the listener some minutes.
branches.cn: 代价线：每句插话都要让听者付出一段时间。

intro.en: Interruption is inter- plus the root rupt- "break" and the noun ending -ion.
intro.cn: interruption 由 inter- 加词根 rupt-「折断」与名词词尾 -ion 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin interruptio and rumpere are recorded; the family also gives English eruption.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 interruptio 与 rumpere 均有记载，这一族也给英语带来 eruption。

items.example: It sets the break in the middle.
The root runs through rupture and abrupt.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根贯穿 rupture 与 abrupt。

items.example: The noun is the direct source.
It makes the verb into a noun.
The verb is the base of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是名词的基础。

items.example: It forms abrupt, broken away suddenly.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abrupt，意为突然断开。

definition_zh: 焦虑地；担忧地；急切地
definition_en: in a worried and uneasy way, or with eager impatience
core_image: 不停朝门口张望的脚步
scene: 车晚点了，站台上的人一次次探头看铁轨尽头。 She waited anxiously for the delayed train.
sceneCN: 这里 anxiously 是「焦急地」（第 1 个义项：带着担忧地做某事）；句意是她焦急地等着晚点的火车。

pos.zh: 副词：焦虑地；担忧地；急切地

senses.title: In a worried way
senses.definition: in a manner that shows unease about what may happen
senses.definitionCN: 以表现出对可能发生之事不安的方式
senses.example: She waited anxiously for the delayed train.
senses.exampleCN: 她焦急地等着晚点的火车。
senses.why: The -ly ending turns the adjective of inner tension into a description of how a person acts while that tension is showing.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ly 把表示内心紧绷的形容词变成描述动作的方式，也就是把这种紧绷表现给人看时的样子。

senses.title: With eager impatience
senses.definition: in a way that shows strong eagerness for something to happen
senses.definitionCN: 以表现出强烈盼望某事发生的方式
senses.example: He anxiously checked the results page every few minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 他每隔几分钟就急切地刷新成绩页面。
senses.why: Since anxious can mean eager, the adverb also describes hurried, impatient action rather than fear.
senses.whyCN: 既然 anxious 可以表示渴望，这个副词也用来描述匆忙而不耐烦的举动，而不是恐惧。

intro.en: Anxiously is anxious plus the native adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: anxiously 是 anxious 加本族语副词词尾 -ly 构成。

items.en: angere meant 'to squeeze'.
items.cn: angere 意为「挤压」。

items.en: anxius meant 'uneasy'.
items.cn: anxius 意为「不安的」。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个形容词。

items.en: The adverb anxiously was formed with -ly.
items.cn: 副词 anxiously 由 -ly 构成。

items.en: It now covers both worried waiting and eager checking.
items.cn: 现代用法兼指焦虑的等待与急切的查看。

note.en: The look-alike group is the anxiety family; the near-meaning group gives other adverbs of unease.
note.cn: 形近组是焦虑词族；近义组是其他表示不安的副词。

entries.definition: worried or eager
a state of worry
with severe pain
in a jumpy way
in a troubled way
with keen desire

normalIntro.en: Anxiously shows the tight feeling in the way someone moves.
normalIntro.cn: anxiously 把紧绷的感觉表现在动作里。

normal.en: Anxious is the adjective; add -ly for the adverb.
normal.cn: anxious 是形容词，加 -ly 得到副词。

normal.en: Wait anxiously and ask anxiously are the commonest pairs.
normal.cn: wait anxiously 与 ask anxiously 是最常见的搭配。

normal.en: The adverb can mean eagerly, not only fearfully.
normal.cn: 这个副词也能表示急切，不只是害怕。

normal.en: Keep the x sound: ANK-shus-ly.
normal.cn: 保留 x 的读音：ANK-shus-ly。

normal.en: Do not write anxiouslly; there is only one l before y.
normal.cn: 不要写成 anxiouslly，y 前只有一个 l。

abstract.en: See footsteps turning at every sound.
abstract.cn: 想象每有声响就转身的脚步。

abstract.en: See a head leaning out over a platform edge.
abstract.cn: 想象有人探出头望向站台尽头。

abstract.en: See a page refreshed again and again.
abstract.cn: 想象页面被反复刷新。

examples.en: She waited anxiously for the delayed train.
examples.cn: 她焦急地等着晚点的火车。

examples.en: He anxiously checked the results page every few minutes.
examples.cn: 他每隔几分钟就急切地刷新成绩页面。

examples.en: The mother looked anxiously at the sleeping child.
examples.cn: 母亲不安地看着熟睡的孩子。

dict_mnemonic.text: anxious（焦虑的）加 -ly（……地）：焦虑地。

root: 由形容词 anxious 加副词词尾 -ly 构成；anxious 源于拉丁语 anxius「不安的」，再上溯到 angere「挤压」。

sensesIntro.en: One adverb covers worried waiting and eager checking.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个副词同时覆盖焦虑的等待与急切的查看。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person turning toward the door at every sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：每有声响就转向门口的人。

branches.en: wait anxiously
branches.cn: 焦急等待

branches.en: look anxiously at the clock
branches.cn: 不安地看钟

branches.en: ask anxiously
branches.cn: 焦急地问

branches.en: anxiously await a reply
branches.cn: 急切等待回复

branches.en: check anxiously
branches.cn: 急切地查看

intro.en: A regular -ly adverb on a Latin adjective of tension.
intro.cn: 这是一个规则的 -ly 副词，建立在表示紧绷的拉丁形容词上。

latinIntro.en: The Latin squeeze root appears inside anxious and anxiety.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语「挤压」词根藏在 anxious 与 anxiety 之中。

definition_zh: 轻轻地；少量地；轻率地；单薄地
definition_en: with little force; in a small amount; without serious attention; or wearing little
core_image: 指尖像羽毛一样落在表面，几乎没有压下去
scene: 清晨的粥只撒了一小撮盐，味道刚刚好。 The cook seasoned the soup lightly and let it simmer.
sceneCN: 这里是「少量地、轻微地」（第 2 个义项：用量或程度小）；句意为厨师只给汤里淡淡地调了味，然后让它小火慢炖。图中可辨识物件：汤锅、盐罐、木勺。

pos.zh: 轻轻地；少量地；轻率地；单薄地

derivatives.zh: 由 light 加表示性质的名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「轻；轻盈」
由 light 加动词后缀 -en 构成，义为「减轻；使明亮」
由 light 与 headed 复合而成，义为「头昏眼花的」

senses.title: With little force
senses.definition: touching or moving something with very little force or weight
senses.definitionCN: 用很小的力气或分量去触碰、移动某物
senses.example: She touched the wet paint lightly with one finger.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一个手指轻轻碰了碰没干的油漆。
senses.why: The adjective light means not heavy, and the -ly ending turns that quality into the manner of an action.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 light 意为「不重」，加上 -ly 词尾，就把这种性质变成动作的方式。

senses.title: In a small amount
senses.definition: using only a small amount of something such as salt or seasoning
senses.definitionCN: 只使用很少的量，例如盐或调味料
senses.example: The soup was lightly salted and tasted fresh.
senses.exampleCN: 这汤只撒了少许盐，尝起来很清爽。
senses.why: A light hand puts on little, so the adverb measures quantity as well as force.
senses.whyCN: 下手轻就是放得少，所以这个副词不只量力气，也量数量。

senses.title: Without serious attention
senses.definition: treating something as unimportant or not worth serious thought
senses.definitionCN: 把某事当成不重要、不值得认真对待
senses.example: Such a warning should not be taken lightly.
senses.exampleCN: 这样的警告不该被当成耳旁风。
senses.why: Something taken light is given no weight, and in English weight stands for seriousness, so the adverb moves from the hand to the mind.
senses.whyCN: 被「轻」拿的东西没有被压上重量，而英语里重量代表认真，于是这个副词从手上滑到了心里。

senses.title: With little clothing or build
senses.definition: wearing few or thin clothes, or having a small and light body
senses.definitionCN: 穿得少或穿得薄，或身材小而轻
senses.example: He was lightly dressed for such a cold morning.
senses.exampleCN: 这么冷的早晨，他穿得实在太单薄。
senses.why: The sense of not heavy applies to clothes and bodies, so the adverb can describe how little a person wears or carries.
senses.whyCN: 「不重」的意思也能用在衣物与身体上，于是这个副词可以形容一个人穿得少、负担轻。

intro.en: Lightly is the adjective for little weight turned into an adverb; it is a Germanic word and not the same light that names brightness.
intro.cn: lightly 是表示「分量轻」的形容词变成的副词；它出自日耳曼语，与那个表示「明亮」的 light 并不是同一个词。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning light in weight and quick in movement is proposed behind this family, though the exact shape is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为这个词族背后有个表示「分量轻、动作快」的原始印欧语词根，具体形式不确定。

items.en: The Germanic adjective meant light in weight and therefore easy to carry or bear.
items.cn: 日耳曼语的形容词意为分量轻，因此也指容易拿、容易承受。

items.en: Old English had two words of this shape: one meant not heavy, the other meant bright, and only the first is behind lightly.
items.cn: 古英语有两个同形词：一个意为不重，一个意为明亮；只有前一个才是 lightly 的来源。

items.en: The adverb ending -lice became -ly, and lightly kept the sense of a small weight or a gentle manner.
items.cn: 副词词尾 -lice 变成 -ly，lightly 保留了小重量与温和方式的意思。

items.en: Modern English also uses lightly for small amounts, for a lack of seriousness and for thin clothing.
items.cn: 现代英语还用 lightly 表示少量、不认真以及穿得单薄。

note.en: The first group collects the weight family and one word that merely looks similar; the second collects adverbs of gentle force or small degree.
note.cn: 第一组收表示「轻」的词族，以及一个只是拼写相近的词；第二组收表示轻柔力道或程度小的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective for not heavy, from which the adverb is built.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「不重」的形容词，副词就是由它构成的。

entries.definition: The quality of being light in weight.
To make something lighter in weight or less serious.
entries.definitionCN: 使重量减轻，或使负担、气氛变轻。

entries.definition: Small in degree; it only looks close to light in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 程度小的；只是拼写与 light 相近，来源不同。

entries.definition: In a soft and careful way, without force.
With low force or low sound.
A little; to a small degree, close to lightly in the sense of amount.
entries.definitionCN: 稍微；程度上小，与 lightly 的「少量」义接近。

normalIntro.en: Lightly is the weight word plus an adverb ending, and it keeps the idea of a small load in the hand, on the tongue and in the mind.
normalIntro.cn: lightly 是表示重量的词加副词词尾，它在手上、在舌尖、在心里都保留「负担很小」的意思。

normal.en: Lightly is light plus -ly, so the adjective for not heavy becomes the adverb for a gentle action.
normal.cn: lightly 是 light 加 -ly，表示「不重」的形容词变成了表示动作轻柔的副词。

normal.en: English has two lights, one of weight and one of brightness, and lightly comes from the first.
normal.cn: 英语有两个 light，一个指重量，一个指亮度，lightly 来自前一个。

normal.en: Lightly salted means a light hand with the salt, not a bright taste.
normal.cn: lightly salted 指撒盐的手很轻，而不是味道明亮。

normal.en: To take something lightly is to give it no weight, which is why the phrase means not serious.
normal.cn: take something lightly 就是不给它重量，所以这个说法意为不认真。

normal.en: Lightly dressed describes thin clothes, because weight and clothing share the same scale.
normal.cn: lightly dressed 形容衣服穿得薄，因为重量与衣装在同一个尺度上。

abstract.en: Lightness is both a fact about grams and a judgement about importance, and the adverb carries both.
abstract.cn: 轻既是一个关于克数的事实，也是一种关于重要性的判断，而这个副词两者都带着。

abstract.en: A light touch leaves the surface almost unchanged, which is why the word so often means care rather than weakness.
abstract.cn: 轻的触碰几乎不改变表面，所以这个词常表示细心，而不是无力。

abstract.en: One adverb moves from fingers to salt to warnings to clothes, and each step keeps the same small weight.
abstract.cn: 一个副词从指尖走到盐，再走到警告与衣服，每一步都保持同样的小小分量。

examples.en: She touched the wet paint lightly with one finger.
examples.cn: 她用一个手指轻轻碰了碰没干的油漆。

examples.en: The soup was lightly salted and tasted fresh.
examples.cn: 这汤只撒了少许盐，尝起来很清爽。

examples.en: Such a warning should not be taken lightly.
examples.cn: 这样的警告不该被当成耳旁风。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来特利」——来的时候特别轻，落脚也很轻；lightly 是轻轻地。

root: 由形容词 light（轻的，古英语 lēoht，与表示「明亮」的 lēoht 同形但不同源）加副词词尾 -ly 构成；一般认为更早的形式出自日耳曼语表示「分量轻」的形容词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a small weight or a gentle manner; the senses spread from touch to amount, to seriousness and to clothing.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是分量小或方式温和；义项从触碰扩展到用量，再到认真程度与衣着。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fingertip landing on a surface like a feather, barely pressing.
core.cn: 核心意象：指尖像羽毛一样落在表面，几乎没有压下去。

branches.en: a finger testing wet paint
branches.cn: 手指试探没干的油漆

branches.en: a pinch of salt falling into a pot
branches.cn: 一小撮盐落进锅里

branches.en: a warning waved away with a shrug
branches.cn: 一个警告被耸肩挥开

branches.en: a thin coat on a cold morning
branches.cn: 冷早晨里的一件薄外套

branches.en: a cook stirring with a light hand
branches.cn: 厨师下手很轻地搅动

intro.en: A Germanic adjective of little weight, an Old English adverb ending, and two endings that turn the quality into a noun and a verb.
intro.cn: 一个表示分量轻的日耳曼形容词、一个古英语副词词尾，以及两个把这种性质变成名词与动词的词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin adjective levis means light in weight and is generally treated as a distant cognate of the Germanic word behind lightly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形容词 levis 意为分量轻，一般认为它与 lightly 背后的日耳曼词是远亲。

definition_zh: 针；缝衣针；注射针；指针；针叶；刺激；激怒
definition_en: a thin pointed tool used for sewing; a hollow needle used to give medicine; the pointer of an instrument; a thin leaf of a pine; and, as a verb, to provoke or tease someone
core_image: 一根细亮的钢针穿过布面，针眼里拖着一根线
scene: 台灯下，奶奶把线头在嘴边抿湿，一次次往针眼里送，终于穿了过去。 She threaded the needle on the third try and began mending the torn sleeve.
sceneCN: 这里「needle」是「缝衣针」（第 1 个义项：用来缝纫的细长尖针）；句意是她第三次才把线穿进针眼，随后开始补破掉的袖子。图中可辨识物件：台灯、线团、针眼、破袖口。

pos.zh: 针；缝衣针；注射针；指针；针叶

collocations.zh: 草垛里的针；极难找到的东西

derivatives.zh: 由 needle 与 work 复合而成，义为「针线活」
由 needle 与 point 复合而成，义为「针绣；针尖绣」
由 needle 与 craft 复合而成，义为「缝纫手艺」

senses.title: A thin pointed tool for sewing
senses.definition: a very thin piece of metal with a sharp point and a hole for thread, used to sew
senses.definitionCN: 细长、一端尖锐、另一端有穿线孔的金属缝纫工具
senses.example: She threaded the needle on the third try.
senses.exampleCN: 她试到第三次才把线穿进针眼。
senses.why: Old English nǣdl named the sewing tool first, and its long vowel and older consonant survive in the modern spelling.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 nǣdl 最早指的就是缝纫工具，它的长元音与更古老的辅音都留在现代拼写里。

senses.title: A hollow needle used to give medicine
senses.definition: a thin hollow tube with a sharp end, fitted to a syringe for injecting or drawing liquid
senses.definitionCN: 装在注射器上、末端尖锐的细空心管，用来注射或抽取液体
senses.example: The nurse fitted a new needle to the syringe.
senses.exampleCN: 护士给注射器换上了一枚新针头。
senses.why: A sewing needle is solid, a medical needle is hollow, but both pierce cleanly, so English reused the older word instead of inventing another.
senses.whyCN: 缝衣针是实心的，医用针是空心的，但两者都能干净地刺穿，所以英语直接沿用旧词，而没有另造新词。

senses.title: The pointer of an instrument
senses.definition: the thin moving pointer on a compass, meter or gauge that shows a reading
senses.definitionCN: 罗盘、仪表或量规上会摆动、用来指示读数的细长指针
senses.example: The compass needle swung north as soon as the lid opened.
senses.exampleCN: 盖子一打开，罗盘指针就转向北方。
senses.why: A compass pointer is a thin sliver of metal that turns freely; its shape matches the sewing tool closely enough for the name to travel.
senses.whyCN: 罗盘指针是一片能自由转动的细金属薄片，形状与缝衣针足够相似，于是名字就迁了过去。

senses.title: A thin leaf of a pine or fir
senses.definition: one of the long thin leaves of a pine tree or a similar evergreen
senses.definitionCN: 松树或类似常绿树上细长的叶子
senses.example: Pine needles covered the path in a soft brown layer.
senses.exampleCN: 松针在路面上铺了软软的一层褐色。
senses.why: An evergreen leaf is long, narrow and sharply pointed, so English reached again for the tool that looks the same.
senses.whyCN: 常绿树的叶子细长而尖，英语便又一次借用了形状相同的那个工具名。

senses.title: To provoke or tease someone
senses.definition: to annoy or provoke someone deliberately, often by repeated small comments
senses.definitionCN: 故意惹恼或刺激某人，常靠反复的小话
senses.example: He kept needling his brother about the lost match.
senses.exampleCN: 他一直拿输掉的比赛去刺激弟弟。
senses.why: A needle is a small sharp thing that goes in and stings; the verb keeps that picture for remarks that prick without wounding deeply.
senses.whyCN: 针是扎进去就会刺痛的小尖物；这个动词保留同一画面，用来形容扎人却不深的小话。

intro.en: Needle goes back to a Germanic word for a sewing tool, and its Latin cousin confirms an old root for spinning and sewing.
intro.cn: needle 可追到日耳曼语中表示缝纫工具的词，它的拉丁远亲也印证了一个表示纺与缝的古老词根。

items.en: A root meaning to sew or spin, reconstructed with an initial s that Germanic loses, is generally accepted.
items.cn: 一般认为有一个表示「缝、纺」的词根，重构形式带一个在日耳曼语中消失的 s。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic form nēþlō named a sewing needle and kept the long vowel.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语形式 nēþlō 指缝衣针，并保留了长元音。

items.en: Old English nǣdl kept a long vowel and a d that stands in for an older þ sound.
items.cn: 古英语 nǣdl 保留长元音，并用 d 代替更古老的 þ 音。

items.en: Middle English wrote nedle, and the modern spelling settled the silent e at the end.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 nedle，现代拼写最终定下末尾不发音的 e。

items.en: Modern English extends needle to the pointer of an instrument, the leaf of a pine, and a verb for provocation.
items.cn: 现代英语把 needle 扩展到仪表指针、松针，以及表示刺激的动词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds built on the same tool; the near-meaning group collects tools that pierce and the acts they perform.
note.cn: 形近组收建在同一件工具上的复合词；近义组收能刺穿的工具及相应动作。

entries.definition: Sewing or embroidery done with a needle.
entries.definitionCN: 用针完成的缝纫或刺绣。

entries.definition: A kind of embroidery worked on canvas with counted stitches.
entries.definitionCN: 在帆布上按格数针的刺绣。

entries.definition: The skill or activity of sewing by hand.
entries.definitionCN: 手工缝纫的技艺或活动。

entries.definition: A short thin metal object with a point, used to fasten cloth.
entries.definitionCN: 固定布料用的短细金属尖物。

entries.definition: A pointed tool for making small holes in leather or wood.
entries.definitionCN: 在皮革或木头上打小孔的尖锥。

entries.definition: A tube with a hollow needle and a plunger, used to inject or withdraw liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 带空心针头和推杆、用于注射或抽液的管子。

normalIntro.en: One ancient tool name, reused wherever something is thin and piercing, is the pattern behind every sense of this word.
normalIntro.cn: 一个古老的工具名，只要遇上是细而尖的东西就再借一次，这就是这个词所有义项背后的规律。

normal.en: Old English nǣdl had a long vowel, and the modern spelling still shows it.
normal.cn: 古英语 nǣdl 带长元音，现代拼写仍能看出这一痕迹。

normal.en: The Latin verb nere, to spin or weave, is the distant cousin that confirms the old sewing root.
normal.cn: 拉丁语动词 nere 意为纺、织，是印证古老缝纫词根的远亲。

normal.en: Needlework and needlepoint are compounds, and both keep the tool visible inside the longer word.
normal.cn: needlework 与 needlepoint 是复合词，两者都把工具留在较长的词里。

normal.en: A needle in a haystack works as an idiom because finding one thin pin in loose straw is nearly impossible.
normal.cn: a needle in a haystack 能成为习语，是因为在松散的草垛里找一根细针几乎不可能。

normal.en: To needle someone takes the sharp little stab and turns it into a repeated remark.
normal.cn: needle 某人把那种小小的刺扎变成了反复说的话。

abstract.en: A needle does its work by passing through, which is why the word can name both joining and piercing.
abstract.cn: 针靠穿过去来做事，所以这个词既能指连接，也能指刺穿。

abstract.en: Pine needles and compass needles share a name with the sewing tool because all three are narrow, pointed and precise.
abstract.cn: 松针、罗盘指针与缝衣针同名，因为三者都细、尖、准。

abstract.en: A remark that needles leaves almost no visible mark, yet it makes the other person flinch.
abstract.cn: 扎人的话几乎不留看得见的痕，却能让对方一缩。

examples.en: She threaded the needle on the third try.
examples.cn: 她试到第三次才把线穿进针眼。

examples.en: The nurse fitted a new needle to the syringe.
examples.cn: 护士给注射器换上了一枚新针头。

examples.en: He kept needling his brother about the lost match.
examples.cn: 他一直拿输掉的比赛去刺激弟弟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尼斗」——针眼小得像斗口，线要斗进去；记住 needle 是针，也是拿话刺人。

root: 古英语 nǣdl（缝衣针），一般认为源自原始日耳曼语 nēþlō，更早可追到表示「缝、纺」的原始印欧语词根；拉丁语 nere（纺、织）是同源远亲。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a thin pointed tool; the senses divide into sewing, medicine, instruments, evergreen leaves, and the small sting of teasing words.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一件细而尖的工具；义项分出缝纫、医疗、仪表、常绿树叶，以及话语扎人的那点刺痛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin steel point passing through cloth, dragging a thread behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚细钢针穿过布面，身后拖着一根线。

branches.en: a thread licked and pushed through a tiny hole
branches.cn: 线头抿湿后被推进小小的针眼

branches.en: a syringe fitted with a fresh tip
branches.cn: 注射器装上新针头

branches.en: a compass pointer turning to the north
branches.cn: 罗盘指针转向北方

branches.en: a path covered with fallen pine leaves
branches.cn: 小路铺满落下的松针

branches.en: a brother wincing at one more teasing remark
branches.cn: 弟弟又被一句玩笑刺得皱眉

intro.en: An Old English tool noun, an English verb, its endings, and two compounds carry the word's history.
intro.cn: 一个古英语工具名词、一个英语动词、它的词尾，以及两个复合词承载了这个词的历史。

latinIntro.en: Latin nere, to spin or weave, is generally treated as a cognate from the same root, so it is listed as a distant relative rather than a source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nere 意为纺、织，一般认为与这个词同出一个词根，所以列为远亲而非来源。

definition_zh: 使受害；迫害；歧视对待
definition_en: to treat someone badly or unfairly, especially because of who they are
core_image: 一群人围着一个人，把过错全推到他身上
scene: 办公室里丢了钱，几个人不查清楚就把新来的实习生叫去问话。 The older staff victimized the new intern over a missing wallet.
sceneCN: 这里 victimize 是「使受害、迫害」（第 1 个义项：因对方的身份或处境而恶意对待某人）；句意为老员工因一只不见的钱包就把新实习生当成了替罪羊。

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -ization 构成，义为「受害；迫害」
加后缀 -er 构成，义为「迫害者」
去后缀 -ize 构成的名词，义为「受害者」

senses.title: To treat someone unfairly and make them suffer
senses.definition: to harm someone repeatedly or unfairly, often because they are weaker
senses.definitionCN: 因对方较弱或不同而反复不公地伤害某人
senses.example: The older staff victimized the new intern over a missing wallet.
senses.exampleCN: 老员工因一只不见的钱包就把新实习生当成了替罪羊。
senses.why: The verb takes the noun victim and adds the doing suffix -ize: to make a victim of someone.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词由名词 victim 加「使之」后缀 -ize 构成，即让某人成为受害者。

senses.title: To single people out for unequal treatment
senses.definition: to treat a group differently and worse than others in an official or everyday setting
senses.definitionCN: 在制度或日常场合中把某一群体区别对待得更差
senses.example: Employers who victimize older applicants face heavy fines.
senses.exampleCN: 歧视年长求职者的雇主会面临重罚。
senses.why: When unfairness follows a whole group rather than one person, the same verb names the practice.
senses.whyCN: 当不公针对的不是一个人而是一整个群体时，用的仍是这个动词。

senses.title: To make someone a victim on purpose
senses.definition: to cause someone to become a victim through a deliberate act
senses.definitionCN: 通过有意的行为使某人成为受害者
senses.example: The gang victimized shopkeepers who paid no protection money.
senses.exampleCN: 团伙把不交保护费的店主当成了整治对象。
senses.why: Any deliberate act that puts a person in the victim’s place fits the transitive verb.
senses.whyCN: 任何有意把人推到受害者位置上的行为，都符合这个及物动词的用法。

senses.title: To blame or punish someone for others’ faults
senses.definition: to make a person carry the blame or the cost of what others did
senses.definitionCN: 让别人承担他人行为造成的过错或代价
senses.example: Do not victimize the messenger for bad news.
senses.exampleCN: 不要因为坏消息就迁怒于报信的人。
senses.why: Blaming a bystander turns him into a victim even when no violence is involved.
senses.whyCN: 把责任推给旁观者，即使没有暴力，也把他变成了受害者。

senses.title: In law, to harm someone for reporting wrongdoing
senses.definition: to treat a person badly because they have complained, reported, or testified
senses.definitionCN: 因某人投诉、举报或作证而对其加以恶待
senses.example: The firm victimized the clerk who reported the safety fault.
senses.exampleCN: 公司报复了举报安全隐患的那名职员。
senses.why: Employment law needed a short verb for punishment that follows a complaint.
senses.whyCN: 劳动法需要一个简短动词来指投诉之后遭到的惩罚。

intro.en: Victimize is a modern formation: the noun victim plus the verb ending -ize.
intro.cn: victimize 是近代构词：名词 victim 加动词词尾 -ize。

items.en: Victima named a creature offered in sacrifice.
items.cn: victima 指用于献祭的活物。

items.en: French victime named the person destroyed by another.
items.cn: 法语 victime 指被他人毁灭的人。

items.en: The noun victim entered English and settled on the harmed party.
items.cn: 名词 victim 进入英语，固定在受损一方身上。

items.en: The suffix -ize, from Greek -izein through Latin, formed verbs meaning to make.
items.cn: -ize 词尾经拉丁语来自希腊语 -izein，构成「使之」类动词。

items.en: The verb victimize appeared in the nineteenth century, meaning to make a victim of.
items.cn: 动词 victimize 出现于十九世纪，义为「使某人成为受害者」。

note.en: The first group holds the victim family, the second lines up persecute, oppress, and the neutral harm.
note.cn: 第一组是 victim 词族，第二组排开 persecute、oppress 与中性的 harm。

entries.definition: a person who is harmed
the act of making victims
the one who makes victims
having no victim
to treat someone cruelly over time
to rule others harshly and unjustly
to frighten a weaker person
to keep someone from harm

normalIntro.en: Add -ize to victim and the noun becomes an action: to put someone in the place of the harmed.
normalIntro.cn: victim 加 -ize，名词就成了动作：把人放进受害者的位置。

normal.en: Victimize, realize, and modernize all share the -ize ending.
normal.cn: victimize、realize、modernize 都共用 -ize 词尾。

normal.en: Victimization adds -ization, like realization.
normal.cn: victimization 加的是 -ization，如同 realization。

normal.en: The person who does it is the victimizer.
normal.cn: 施加迫害的人是 victimizer。

normal.en: Feel victimized is common in reports of unfair treatment.
normal.cn: 感到受了不公对待时常说 feel victimized。

normal.en: The stress stays on the first syllable: VIC-ti-mize.
normal.cn: 重音仍在第一音节：VIC-ti-mize。

abstract.en: Picture a group stepping back so one person falls.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人齐齐后退，让一个人摔下去。

abstract.en: See a name circled on a list while others are left alone.
abstract.cn: 想一张名单上只有一个名字被圈出来。

abstract.en: Hear a manager say the fault is always this worker’s.
abstract.cn: 听经理说，错总是这一个人的。

examples.en: The union says the company victimized workers who spoke up.
examples.cn: 工会称公司报复了敢于发声的工人。

examples.en: Children who are victimized at school often hide it.
examples.cn: 在学校受欺凌的孩子常把事瞒着。

examples.en: No law lets an employer victimize a pregnant applicant.
examples.cn: 没有任何法律允许雇主歧视怀孕的求职者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维克厅埋子」——维克厅为了掩盖旧事，把知情的孩子迫害了。

root: 拉丁语 victima（献祭的活物）→ 法语 victime → victim + -ize（使…）→ victimize

sensesIntro.en: One verb covers unfair treatment of a person, of a group, of a scapegoat, and of anyone punished for speaking out.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个动词覆盖了对个人、对群体、对替罪者，以及对举报者的不公对待。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd pushing the blame onto one person.
core.cn: 核心意象：一群人把过错推给一个人。

branches.en: The unfair branch: staff turning on an intern.
branches.cn: 不公分支：员工一同针对实习生。

branches.en: The group branch: older applicants shut out.
branches.cn: 群体分支：年长求职者被拒。

branches.en: The gang branch: shopkeepers picked as targets.
branches.cn: 团伙分支：店主被当作目标。

branches.en: The scapegoat branch: blaming the messenger.
branches.cn: 替罪分支：迁怒报信人。

branches.en: The law branch: payback for a report.
branches.cn: 法律分支：因举报而遭报复。

intro.en: The stem victim- plus the verb suffix -ize yields the base verb; -ization, -er, and -less extend the family.
intro.cn: 词干 victim- 加动词后缀 -ize 构成基础动词，再以 -ization、-er、-less 扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin victima has no clear relatives; the productive suffix -ize is what gives the word its action.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 victima 缺乏明确亲缘，真正赋予动作义的是能产后缀 -ize。

items.example: Victim- is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: victim- 是这个词族的词基。

items.example: Victimize means to make a victim.
items.exampleCN: victimize 意为使某人成为受害者。

items.example: A victimless crime has no harmed party.
items.exampleCN: 无受害者犯罪没有受损一方。

items.example: The victimized clerk was moved to another office.
items.exampleCN: 被报复的职员被调到另一间办公室。
persecute 强调持续追打的运动。

items.example: Oppress stresses the weight of power.
The law exists to protect, not to victimize.
items.exampleCN: 法律的存在是为了保护，而不是使人受害。

definition_zh: 手掌；掌心；棕榈树；把…藏于掌中；骗卖
definition_en: the inner surface of the hand, a tropical tree with a crown of large fanning leaves, and to hide something small in the hand or pass it off on someone
core_image: 一只摊开的手，掌纹向四周散开，像撑开的扇叶
scene: 庙会的老先生摊开手，让围着的孩子看他掌心的纹路。 The old man turned his hand over and showed us the lines on his palm.
sceneCN: 这里 palm 是「手掌、掌心」（第 1 个义项：手的内侧面）；句意为老人把手翻过来，让我们看他掌心的纹路。图中可辨识物件：摊开的手掌、庙会的灯笼、围观的孩子。

collocations.phrase: in the palm of one's hand
collocations.zh: 在某人的掌心里；完全受其掌控

derivatives.zh: palm 加表示「从事某事的人」的后缀 -ist，指看手相的人
palm 加表示技艺的后缀 -istry，指看手相的方术
palm 加 -y 构成，先指多棕榈的，再引申为繁荣兴旺的

senses.title: The inner surface of the hand
senses.definition: the inner surface of the hand, from the wrist to the base of the fingers
senses.definitionCN: 手的内侧面，从手腕一直到手指根部
senses.example: The old man turned his hand over and showed us the lines on his palm.
senses.exampleCN: 老人把手翻过来，让我们看他掌心的纹路。
senses.why: Latin palma first named this flat, open surface, so the word begins at the body part whenever a hand is held out or turned upward.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 palma 最初就指这块平坦、张开的表面，所以只要把手摊开或翻向上，这个词就从身体部位开始。

senses.title: A tropical tree with fanning leaves
senses.definition: a tropical tree with a tall trunk and a crown of large leaves spreading from one point
senses.definitionCN: 一种热带树木，树干高大，大叶子从同一点向四周展开
senses.example: A row of palms shaded the road along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 海岸公路旁一排棕榈树投下阴凉。
senses.why: The fronds of many palms spread from one point like the fingers of an open hand, so Latin reused palma for the tree and English kept both senses.
senses.whyCN: 许多棕榈的叶片从同一点向外张开，像摊开的手指向四周，拉丁语就把 palma 也给了这种树，英语把两个义项都留了下来。

senses.title: To hide something in the hand
senses.definition: to hide a small object in the closed hand, especially to deceive someone
senses.definitionCN: 把一个小东西藏在合起的手里，尤指为了骗人
senses.example: He palmed the coin and slipped it into his sleeve.
senses.exampleCN: 他把硬币扣在掌心，顺手滑进了袖口。
senses.why: Once palm names the part of the hand others cannot see when it closes, the verb can name the trick of keeping an object there while everyone watches.
senses.whyCN: 既然 palm 指手合拢后别人看不见的那一面，动词就能指「在众目之下把东西留在那里」的手法。

senses.title: To pass something off on someone
senses.definition: to get rid of something by persuading someone that it is better than it is
senses.definitionCN: 靠让人相信某物比实际更好，从而把东西脱手
senses.example: The dealer palmed off a fake watch on a tourist.
senses.exampleCN: 那个商贩把一块假表骗卖给了游客。
senses.why: The hand that conceals can also pass something on unseen, so palm off names a deal finished before the other person has had a proper look.
senses.whyCN: 会藏东西的手也能把东西悄悄递出去，所以 palm off 指一笔在对方看清之前就已成交的买卖。

intro.en: Palm goes back to Latin palma, which named both the flat of the hand and the tree whose leaves spread like fingers; Old English borrowed it for the tree and the hand.
intro.cn: palm 出自拉丁语 palma，这个词既指手掌的平面，也指叶片像手指一样张开的树；古英语把两个意思都借了进来。

items.en: Palma named the flat inner surface of the hand, the part held open or used to strike.
items.cn: palma 指手内那一块平坦的表面，也就是摊开或用来拍打的那一面。

items.en: The same word was given to the date palm because its fronds fan out from one point like an open hand.
items.cn: 同一个词也被给了枣椰树，因为它的叶丛从同一点张开，像一只摊开的手。

items.en: Old English took the word through the church, first for the palm branches carried on Palm Sunday and then for the tree.
items.cn: 古英语经教会借入这个词，先指棕枝主日所持的棕榈枝，再指这种树。

items.en: Middle English kept the hand sense and the tree sense side by side, and also used palm as a unit of length taken from the hand.
items.cn: 中古英语让「手」与「树」两个义项并存，还把 palm 用作以手宽为准的长度单位。

items.en: Modern English keeps palmed and palming, and the phrase palm off for passing something off on someone.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 palmed 与 palming，以及表示「骗卖、塞给别人」的 palm off。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin word for the hand and the tree; the near-meaning group gathers words for hands and for the leaves that look like them.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁语中兼指手掌与棕榈的那个词展开；近义组收表示手以及像手的叶片的词。

entries.definition: A medieval pilgrim who carried a palm branch home from the Holy Land.
entries.definitionCN: 中世纪从圣地朝圣归来、手持棕榈枝的朝圣者。

entries.definition: A person who reads the lines of the hand.
The practice of telling a person's future from the lines of the hand.
entries.definitionCN: 从手掌纹路推测命运的方术。

entries.definition: The whole part of the body at the end of the arm, fingers included.
entries.definitionCN: 手臂末端包含手指的整个部位。

entries.definition: The foot of an animal such as a dog or cat.
A long leaf of a palm or a fern, divided into many parts.
entries.definitionCN: 棕榈或蕨类那种分成许多部分的长叶。

normalIntro.en: One Latin word covers the open hand and the tree that copies its shape, and the family around it keeps folding the hand into a tool of hiding.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拉丁词同时覆盖摊开的手与模仿其形状的树，而它周围的词族不断把这只手折成藏东西的工具。

normal.en: Latin palma is both the open hand and the palm tree, one picture doing two jobs.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 palma 既是摊开的手，也是棕榈树，一幅画面干了两件事。

normal.en: The lines of the palm are what palmistry claims to read.
normal.cn: 掌纹正是 palmistry 声称要读的东西。

normal.en: A palm was once a unit of length measured across the hand.
normal.cn: palm 曾是以手宽丈量的长度单位。

normal.en: The verb palm keeps the hand closed: the coin vanishes inside it.
normal.cn: 动词 palm 让手合起来：硬币就在里面不见了。

normal.en: Palm off adds a direction to that closed hand: the hidden thing is pushed onto someone else.
normal.cn: palm off 给这只合起的手加了方向：藏着的东西被推给了别人。

abstract.en: The palm is the part of the body that can both give and conceal.
abstract.cn: 手掌是身体上既能给予又能藏匿的那一部分。

abstract.en: A tree that looks like an open hand ties the body to the landscape.
abstract.cn: 一棵看起来像摊开的手的树，把身体和风景系在一起。

abstract.en: Whatever fits inside a closed palm is small enough to be denied.
abstract.cn: 能握进掌心的东西，小到可以否认它存在。

examples.en: The old man turned his hand over and showed us the lines on his palm.
examples.cn: 老人把手翻过来，让我们看他掌心的纹路。

examples.en: A row of palms shaded the road along the coast.
examples.cn: 海岸公路旁一排棕榈树投下阴凉。

examples.en: The dealer palmed off a fake watch on a tourist.
examples.cn: 那个商贩把一块假表骗卖给了游客。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「帕姆」——摊开手掌喊一声「帕姆」，记住 palm 是手掌。

root: 拉丁语 palma（手掌），同一个词又指棕榈，因叶丛像摊开的手；经古英语 palm 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the open hand; the senses widen to the tree that copies its shape, then narrow to the closed hand that hides and finally to the hand that cheats.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是摊开的手；义项先扩到形状如手的棕榈，再收拢到藏东西的合掌，最后落到行骗的那只手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open hand whose lines spread outward like the leaves of a fan.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只摊开的手，掌纹向四周散开，像撑开的扇叶。

branches.en: a reader tracing the lines of a palm
branches.cn: 看相人沿掌纹描过去

branches.en: a coast road shaded by tall palms
branches.cn: 被高大棕榈遮荫的海岸公路

branches.en: a coin vanishing inside a closed hand
branches.cn: 硬币在合起的手里消失

branches.en: a fake watch passed to a tourist
branches.cn: 假表被塞给游客

branches.en: leaves that fan out like fingers and a hand that closes
branches.cn: 像手指张开的叶丛与合拢的手

intro.en: The word is a single Latin noun for hand and tree, with English suffixes building the reader, the art and the tree-filled place.
intro.cn: 这个词就是一个兼指手掌与棕榈的拉丁名词，英语后缀在它周围造出看相人、相术和长满棕榈的地方。

latinIntro.en: Latin palma is recorded for both the hand and the tree, and the adjective palmatus describes something shaped or decorated like a hand.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 palma 兼指手掌与棕榈，形容词 palmatus 则描述像手一样张开或以棕榈装饰的东西。

latinEntries.meaning: palm of the hand; palm tree
shaped like a hand, decorated with palms

definition_zh: 望远镜；叠缩；压缩
definition_en: a tube with lenses for seeing distant objects, or to fold one part into another
core_image: 长筒对准夜空中的月亮
scene: 他把望远镜对准夜空中的那轮月亮。 He pointed the telescope at the moon in the night sky.
sceneCN: 这里 telescope 是「望远镜」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他把望远镜对准夜空中的那轮月亮。

senses.title: An instrument for distant viewing
senses.definition: a tube with lenses or mirrors that makes far objects look nearer
senses.definitionCN: 用透镜或镜面把远处物体放大的筒状装置
senses.example: He pointed the telescope at the moon in the night sky.
senses.exampleCN: 他把望远镜对准夜空中的那轮月亮。
senses.why: The Greek parts mean far and look, which describes the instrument exactly.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语两部分意为「远」与「看」，正是这件仪器的描述。

senses.title: To slide one part into another
senses.definition: to fold sections of something so that one slides into the next
senses.definitionCN: 把各段依次套进去以缩短
senses.example: She telescoped the umbrella and stepped inside.
senses.exampleCN: 她收拢雨伞，走进屋里。
senses.why: A telescope pulls out in sections, so pushing them back became the verb.
senses.whyCN: 望远镜由几节拉出，把它推回去的动作就成了动词。

senses.title: To squeeze things together
senses.definition: to make events or objects occupy less space or time
senses.definitionCN: 让事件或物件占据更少的空间或时间
senses.example: The two meetings telescoped into one short hour.
senses.exampleCN: 两场会议被压缩成一个短小时。
senses.why: Sections that slide inside each other become a picture of saving space.
senses.whyCN: 一节节套进去的形象，就是节省空间的比喻。

intro.en: Telescope combines Greek words for far and to look.
intro.cn: telescope 把希腊语中「远」与「看」两词合在一起。

items.en: Tele meant far away.
items.cn: tele 意为遥远。

items.en: Skopein meant to look at.
items.cn: skopein 意为观看。

items.en: Telescopio named the new viewing tube.
items.cn: telescopio 指这种新的观察筒。

items.en: Telescope entered English for the star instrument.
items.cn: telescope 进入英语，指观星装置。

items.en: It also means folding sections together.
items.cn: 它也表示把各节套叠起来。

note.en: Telescope is compared with look-alike forms and with optical instruments.
note.cn: 把 telescope 与形近形式以及光学仪器名作对比。

entries.definition: able to extend
folded together
a far-voice device
an instrument for tiny things
two small telescopes for both eyes
a curved piece that bends light

normalIntro.en: Telescope means far-looking, and its sections slide like its name.
normalIntro.cn: telescope 意为「看远处」，它的各节也像名字一样套缩。

normal.en: He pointed the telescope at the moon.
normal.cn: 他把望远镜对准月亮。

normal.en: She telescoped the umbrella at the door.
normal.cn: 她在门口收拢雨伞。

normal.en: The radio telescope listens to the sky.
normal.cn: 射电望远镜聆听天空。

normal.en: The two meetings telescoped into one hour.
normal.cn: 两场会议压缩成一小时。

normal.en: A space telescope orbits the earth.
normal.cn: 一台空间望远镜绕地球运行。

abstract.en: Far things come near through a tube.
abstract.cn: 远处的事物通过一根筒靠近。

abstract.en: Folding is looking, in a smaller shape.
abstract.cn: 套叠就是以更小的形状「看」。

abstract.en: Space can be pushed into less space.
abstract.cn: 空间可以被压进更小的空间。

examples.en: He pointed the telescope at the moon in the night sky.
examples.cn: 他把望远镜对准夜空中的那轮月亮。

examples.en: She telescoped the umbrella and stepped inside.
examples.cn: 她收拢雨伞，走进屋里。

examples.en: The two meetings telescoped into one short hour.
examples.cn: 两场会议被压缩成一个短小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太远看不见，使个筒」——远处看不清，就使个筒子看，正是望远镜。

root: 希腊语 tele（远）加 skopein（观看）构成，经意大利语 telescopio 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Telescope names the far-seeing tube, then the sliding of its sections, then any compression.
sensesIntro.cn: telescope 先指看远的筒，再指各节套缩，再指任何压缩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long tube pointed at the moon.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根长筒对准月亮。

branches.en: The instrument is the main sense.
branches.cn: 仪器是主要义项。

branches.en: Sliding sections come from the tube.
branches.cn: 套缩动作来自筒身。

branches.en: Compression borrows the same image.
branches.cn: 压缩借用同一形象。

branches.en: Instrument and folding are one design.
branches.cn: 仪器与套叠源于同一设计。

branches.en: Both save space.
branches.cn: 两者都节省空间。

intro.en: Telescope pairs with microscope and other -scope words.
intro.cn: telescope 与 microscope 等 -scope 词并列。

latinIntro.en: The word is Greek in origin; Latin supplies visio for related sight words.
latinIntro.cn: 该词源自希腊语；拉丁语 visio 提供相关「看」的词根。

definition_zh: 伪造；锻造；奋勇前进；建立
definition_en: to make a false copy, to shape metal with heat, to move ahead steadily, or to build a relationship
core_image: 炉火通红，铁锤起落，一块金属被敲出形状
scene: 他伪造了父亲的签名。 He forged his father's signature.
sceneCN: 这里 forge 是「伪造」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他伪造了父亲的签名。

senses.title: To fake
senses.definition: to make an illegal copy of something
senses.definitionCN: 非法制作某物的副本
senses.example: He forged his father's signature.
senses.exampleCN: 他伪造了父亲的签名。
senses.why: This is the most familiar modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代最熟悉的义项。

senses.title: To shape metal
senses.definition: to shape metal by heating and hammering
senses.definitionCN: 通过加热和锤打使金属成形
senses.example: The blacksmith forged a knife by the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 铁匠在炉火旁锻造了一把刀。
senses.why: This is the original craft sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是原本的工艺义项。

senses.title: To move ahead
senses.definition: to move forward steadily and with effort
senses.definitionCN: 稳步而费力地向前推进
senses.example: The team forged ahead despite the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管下雨，队伍仍然奋勇前进。
senses.why: The image of hammering becomes steady effort.
senses.whyCN: 锤打的意象转化为持续的努力。

senses.title: To build
senses.definition: to build something strong, such as a friendship or plan
senses.definitionCN: 建立牢固的事物，如友谊或计划
senses.example: They forged a lasting friendship.
senses.exampleCN: 他们建立了长久的友谊。
senses.why: What is forged is made strong by effort.
senses.whyCN: 锻造之物因努力而坚固。

intro.en: Forge comes through Old French from a Latin word for a workshop.
intro.cn: forge 经古法语来自拉丁语中表示工坊的词。

items.en: Fabrica meant a workshop or craft.
items.cn: fabrica 意为工坊或手艺。

items.en: Forge named a smithy.
items.cn: forge 指铁匠铺。

items.en: Forgen meant to shape metal.
items.cn: forgen 意为锻造金属。

items.en: The word came to mean to fake documents.
items.cn: 这个词逐渐表示伪造文件。

items.en: Forge ahead came to mean to push forward.
items.cn: forge ahead 逐渐表示向前推进。

note.en: Forge is compared with similar-looking words and with words for faking and shaping.
note.cn: 把 forge 与形近词以及表示伪造和成形的词作比较。

strength or power
a tool for eating
to make a false copy
to invent or make something false
to give something a form

normalIntro.en: Forge means to hammer something into shape, whether metal or a lie.
normalIntro.cn: forge 是把东西锤打成形，无论对象是金属还是谎言。

normal.en: He forged his father's signature.
normal.cn: 他伪造了父亲的签名。

normal.en: The blacksmith forged a knife by the fire.
normal.cn: 铁匠在炉火旁锻造了一把刀。

normal.en: The team forged ahead despite the rain.
normal.cn: 尽管下雨，队伍仍然奋勇前进。

normal.en: They forged a lasting friendship.
normal.cn: 他们建立了长久的友谊。

normal.en: The document was clearly forged.
normal.cn: 这份文件显然是伪造的。

abstract.en: Fire and patience make metal honest.
abstract.cn: 火与耐心让金属变得诚实。

abstract.en: A lie is forged with the same care as a blade.
abstract.cn: 谎言和刀刃一样需要精心锻造。

abstract.en: Friendships are forged, not found ready-made.
abstract.cn: 友谊是锻造出来的，不是现成捡来的。

dict_mnemonic.text: forge 原指铁匠铺：在炉火里把铁打成想要的形状，后来把假的文件也「打」得像真的。

root: 经古法语 forge（铁匠铺）源自拉丁语 fabrica（工坊），核心义「加热锤打使成形」。

sensesIntro.en: Forge means to fake, to shape metal, to move ahead, or to build.
sensesIntro.cn: forge 意为伪造、锻造、奋勇前进或建立。

core.en: Heat and force give a thing its shape.
core.cn: 热与力赋予事物形状。

branches.en: A false copy is hammered into shape.
branches.cn: 假副本被锤打成形。

branches.en: Hot metal obeys the hammer.
branches.cn: 热金属听从铁锤。

branches.en: Effort pushes the team forward.
branches.cn: 努力把队伍向前推。

branches.en: Friendship is built by repeated effort.
branches.cn: 友谊由反复努力建成。

branches.en: Real shaping and false shaping share one craft.
branches.cn: 真实的成形与虚假的成形共享同一种手艺。

intro.en: Forge builds a family of smithing and faking words.
intro.cn: forge 构成表示锻造与伪造的词族。

latinIntro.en: Forge comes from Latin fabrica; the Latin entries below show that source.

items.example: The smith can forge a blade.

latinEntries.example: Fabrica is the Latin source of forge.

definition_zh: 指导方针；准则；辅助线
definition_en: a rule or piece of advice about how to do something, or a line that helps you draw
core_image: 一份印着清晰条目的安全准则文件
scene: 公司发布了新的安全指导方针。 The company issued new safety guidelines.
sceneCN: 这里 guideline 是「指导方针」（第 1 个义项）；句意：公司发布了新的安全指导方针。

senses.title: Official rule of advice
senses.definition: an official rule or piece of advice on how to act
senses.definitionCN: 关于如何行动的正式规则或建议
senses.example: The company issued new safety guidelines.
senses.exampleCN: 公司发布了新的安全指导方针。
senses.why: This is the main modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代主要义项。

senses.title: Standard to follow
senses.definition: a standard used to judge or decide something
senses.definitionCN: 用来判断或决定事物的标准
senses.example: The board set clear guidelines for pay.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会为薪酬制定了明确的准则。
senses.why: Advice became a standard of judgment.
senses.whyCN: 建议变成了判断的标准。

senses.title: Drawing aid
senses.definition: a light line drawn to help keep a design straight
senses.definitionCN: 为保持设计平直而画的浅线
senses.example: Erase the guideline after drawing.
senses.exampleCN: 画完后擦掉辅助线。
senses.why: The literal line came first in design work.
senses.whyCN: 设计工作中先有字面意义上的「线」。

intro.en: Guideline joins guide, to lead, with line; the word first named a light drawing line.
intro.cn: guideline 由 guide（引导）与 line（线）组合而成，最初指绘画用的浅线。

items.en: The root of guide meant to show the way.
items.cn: guide 的词根意为指路。

items.en: Guider meant to lead or direct.
items.cn: guider 意为引导、带领。

items.en: Guide named a person who leads.
items.cn: guide 指带路的人。

items.en: Guideline first meant a light drawing line.
items.cn: guideline 最初指绘画的辅助线。

items.en: The sense widened to rules of advice.
items.cn: 词义扩展为指导性的规则。

note.en: Guideline is compared with look-alike words and words for rules.
note.cn: 把 guideline 与形近词以及表示规则的词作比较。

entries.definition: a person who shows the way
help and advice
a person who protects a place

normalIntro.en: A guideline is a line that guides: first on paper, then in policy.
normalIntro.cn: guideline 是一条起引导作用的线：先在纸上，后在制度里。

normal.en: Follow the safety guidelines.
normal.cn: 遵守安全准则。

normal.en: The guidelines are clear.
normal.cn: 这些指导方针很清楚。

normal.en: Set guidelines before you start.
normal.cn: 开始前先定好准则。

normal.en: Draw a guideline first.
normal.cn: 先画一条辅助线。

normal.en: We need guidelines on pay.
normal.cn: 我们需要关于薪酬的准则。

abstract.en: A line on paper keeps the hand steady.
abstract.cn: 纸上的一条线，让手更稳。

abstract.en: Rules are lines drawn for many hands.
abstract.cn: 规则，是为许多只手画下的线。

abstract.en: A guideline guides; it does not carry.
abstract.cn: 准则只是引导，不会替你走。

examples.en: The company issued new safety guidelines.
examples.cn: 公司发布了新的安全指导方针。

examples.en: The board set clear guidelines for pay.
examples.cn: 董事会为薪酬制定了明确的准则。

examples.en: Erase the guideline after drawing.
examples.cn: 画完后擦掉辅助线。

dict_mnemonic.text: guideline 是「指导方针、准则」，也指绘图用的「辅助线」；follow guidelines 是遵循准则，safety guidelines 是安全准则；常用复数。

root: 由 guide（引导）与 line（线）组合而成；最初指绘图时保持平直的辅助线，后引申为行动与判断的指导方针。

sensesIntro.en: Guideline means an official rule of advice, a standard, or a drawing line.
sensesIntro.cn: guideline 指正式的指导方针、判断准则，或绘图辅助线。

core.en: A line that keeps action straight.
core.cn: 让行动保持平直的一条线。

branches.en: A short list sets out each step.
branches.cn: 一张短清单列出每个步骤。

branches.en: A board decides where the limit lies.
branches.cn: 董事会决定界限在哪里。

branches.en: A pale line crosses the paper.
branches.cn: 一条浅线横过纸面。

branches.en: Advice and standard both draw a limit.
branches.cn: 建议与标准，都划出一道界限。

branches.en: The paper line became a rule for people.
branches.cn: 纸上的线，成了人的规则。

intro.en: Guideline forms a plural and links to guide words.
intro.cn: guideline 构成复数，并与 guide 系列词相连。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the parts came through Old French.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，其组成部分经古法语传入。
